# Epigenetic Prediction of Alternative Splicing: Per-Event Models

## What this report asks, and what would count as an answer

One question, asked per alternative-splicing event: **can that event's PSI be predicted from the
epigenetic state of its own locus, beyond what a matched but unrelated locus would predict?**

The "beyond a matched locus" clause carries the whole argument. Chromatin marks, DNA methylation and
gene expression all track **cell-type identity**, and PSI does too. So a model can predict an event's
PSI very well while learning nothing about that event: it learns *which cell type this sample is* and
exploits the fact that PSI differs between cell types. This is the **cell-type fingerprint confound**,
and it is why a high R² is not evidence of epigenetic control of splicing. What separates the two is a
**matched null**: refit the same model on a *different, unrelated* locus's features while keeping this
event's PSI. If the unrelated locus predicts just as well, the signal was fingerprint, not regulation.

This is the analysis the manuscript's "revisiting" framing rests on, so the report is deliberately
ordered so that *null-calibration* evidence comes before any hit list.

## Two tiers, and why the work is split

Significance and interpretation are different jobs wanting different models, so they are separated:

|                | **Tier 1 — screen**                                   | **Tier 2 — elastic net**              |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Question       | *Is* this event predictable beyond its matched null?  | *Which features* carry the signal?    |
| Model          | closed-form ridge partial-R², group-LOO by ontology   | tuned elastic net (glmnet/tidymodels) |
| Runs on        | **every** event (~34k)                                | **hits only**                         |
| Null           | matched control loci (RI 818, SE 200) → p → FDR q     | none (real PSI only)                  |
| Script         | `09s-ridge-screen.R` → `09s-aggregate.R`              | `09-1-ml-local.R` → `09zz-…glmnet….R` |

Tier 1 wants an **omnibus, high-power, closed-form** detector: ridge's L2 penalty aggregates diffuse,
correlated chromatin signal instead of arbitrarily picking one of several collinear windows, and being
closed-form makes a several-hundred-locus null essentially free. Tier 2 wants **sparsity**, because its
deliverable is a short, readable feature list — but sparse selection among collinear features is
unstable, which is exactly why it must not be the thing that decides significance.

A consequence worth stating plainly: **if Tier 1 returns no hits, Tier 2 has nothing to run on** and
every elastic-net section renders empty. That is a real, expected production state, not a failure — see
*How to read a report with no hits* below.

## Feature spaces (and why they are tested separately)

Both tiers use the same three nested spaces:

- **`local`** — event-overlapping regions only
- **`short`** — plus near-vicinity chromHMM windows
- **`long`** — plus far-vicinity chromHMM windows; i.e. all epigenetic features

The two tiers share the *structure* of this partition (the same nested chromHMM split, derived from the
same `chromhmm_hits_smaller` vicinity map) but **not the identical column sets**. Tier 1 partials
protocol, gene expression and TSS distance out as *unpenalised confounds*, while Tier 2 carries them as
ordinary penalised predictors (plus a protocol × expression interaction); and Tier 1 additionally excludes
provenance (`H3K*_source`, i.e. observed-vs-imputed) and QC columns that Tier 2 currently admits. So
compare *rankings* between tiers, not coefficient-for-coefficient membership.

Tier 1 screens **each space separately** and computes FDR **within each
(`transcript_filter`, `Event Type`, `feature_set`) group**. Reason: a signal confined to the exon's
immediate neighbourhood is *diluted* when hundreds of far chromHMM windows go into one omnibus ridge,
so an event with genuine local signal can be missed by `long` and found by `local`.

Two rules follow from the nesting (`local ⊂ short ⊂ long`) and must be respected when reading any table
below:

1. **Never sum per-set hit counts.** The sets are not independent tests of different things; they are
   three views of the same event. An event is a Tier-2 **hit if significant in *any* set**.
2. **Never compare raw R² across sets.** Dropping chromHMM lowers R² mechanically. `effect`
   (`real R² − mean null R²`) *is* comparable, because the matched null drops with it.

## Other conventions

- **Lambda selection** (Tier 2): `min` (lowest CV error) vs `1se` (most regularised model within 1 SE
  of the minimum). `1se` is the conservative read.
- **Expression bias** (Tier 2): a real-PSI model is *Epigenetic Only* if no `gene_expression`-derived
  feature survives robust cross-fold selection, else *Expression Bias*. Gene expression is a confound
  here, not a feature of interest — it co-varies with differentiation state, so an *Expression Bias*
  model's chromatin coefficients cannot be attributed to splicing regulation.
- **CV groups are ontology supergroups**, never random folds — a random split would let the same cell
  type appear in train and test and re-import the fingerprint confound through the back door.
- **`n_robust`** = features selected in *every* CV fold. `has_model == FALSE` means `n_robust == 0`:
  nothing survived, so the event has no interpretable model.

## Document structure (mirrors the order the code runs)

0. **Setup and table construction** — session, Tier-1 screen, Tier-2 per-event tables, and every
   derived table used later. No analysis, no plots.
1. **Tier 1 — the screen.** QC/calibration *first* (is the null honest?), then the significance
   results, then the per-event raw material behind them, and finally the **detection floor** (1.5):
   what effect size this screen could have found. A null result is not interpretable without it.
2. **Tier 2 — elastic net on hits.** How many events got models, which hyperparameters were chosen,
   and fit quality.
3. **What distinguishes significant events?** Variability, feature-count robustness, fold-to-fold
   consistency, lambda stability.
4. **Mark-level analysis.** Which marks are selected, stratified by significance; TSS-proximity
   control.
5. **PSI variability vs model quality.**
6. **Inter-model feature variation** — is mark selection structured across events, or idiosyncratic?

## How to read a report with no hits

**Numbers below are `stat_version` 5** (re-screened 2026-08-21–25 after `09-ml-shared.R`'s ridge λ
selection changed from GCV to exact LOOCV + a 1SE rule — see the version history at
`SCREEN_STAT_VERSION` in that file). They supersede an earlier `stat_version` 4 pass whose figures
this guide previously quoted; re-run `.claude/scratch/verify_09_2_reported_numbers.R` after any future
re-screen; every figure below is checked against it.

If Tier 1 yields no significant events, sections 2–6 are empty by construction (`en_available` is
`FALSE`, those chunks are skipped). The report is still **complete and interpretable** — the evidence
lives in section 1, and it rests on two things:

- a **flat** empirical-p histogram says the null is calibrated, so "no hits" is a real negative result
  rather than a broken test. On the completed screen `p_emp <= 0.05` runs **4.39–5.97%** per
  `(Event Type × feature set)` family against 5% expected, and the floor-free `p_pooled_z` runs
  3.77–6.20% (and 0.056–0.169% at the 0.001 level, vs 0.1% expected) — calibrated under both
  constructions in aggregate, so there is no *reservoir* of signal being lost to multiple testing. A
  p-histogram **piled up at 0** would instead mean the null is optimistic and nothing could be
  concluded. This calibration claim is about the bulk of each family, not about individual events —
  see the pooled-z caveat below;
- the **p gradient across signed-R² strata** (§1.1 check 2's table, cut at 0 / 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.5) is the
  fingerprint signature, and it is cleanest in the two large-*n* families: `median_p` falls
  monotonically as R² rises for **SE/local (0.716 → 0.030) and SE/long (0.522 → 0.127)**. It is
  noisier elsewhere — RI's three families split only ~1,775 tested events across 5 strata (the top
  stratum holds as few as **1** event for RI/short and **0** for RI/long), and SE/short dips
  non-monotonically at its second-highest stratum — so only 2 of the 6 families are strictly monotone
  under this statistic version. Even in the clean SE families the top (`> 0.5`) stratum never
  approaches significance (family min q 0.796 / 0.842). High R² buys almost nothing once the
  comparison is against a matched locus, which is what "fingerprint, not regulation" means
  quantitatively — the claim just now rests on SE's larger families rather than being uniform across
  all six.

**Do not use `effect` (or `mean(screen_R2)`) as that signature.** An earlier version of this guide said
the no-hit fingerprint was `effect ≈ 0` in every raw-R² stratum; the completed screen contradicts it.
`effect = screen_R2 − mean(null_R2)` is mean-based, so the heavy-tailed R² blow-ups documented in §1
corrupt it: it is positive for **79.3%** of rows (vs ~50% under a symmetric null), and the blow-up
fraction itself (`|screen_R2| > 1`) is now **50.1%** of all rows — up from 29.6% under the prior λ
selection, an unexplained side effect of the LOOCV+1SE change worth investigating separately (more
regularization did not reduce out-of-support extrapolation blow-ups; if anything the rate roughly
doubled). Use the rank-based `q` for inference, and `effect_bounded` / `effect_ccc` if a bounded effect
size is wanted.

**The primary hit rule (`q < 0.1`) still gives 0 hits, min q 0.551 (RI/local).** The floor-free
pooled-z sensitivity, which previously agreed with the primary rule at 0 hits, now surfaces **7
candidate events** (min `q_pooled_z` 0.0145) — the two constructions no longer agree, which is exactly
the scenario §1.3 below says to treat as candidates, not hits, pending a calibration check. Of the 7,
2 (small-*n*, `long`-space, `r2_confounds` in the hundreds-to-thousands range) look like the same
confound-projection instability tracked in `09-confound-projection-instability.md`; the other 5 (all
`SE/local`, n = 188–409, self-consistent `r2_confounds`) remain open and are not yet resolved one way
or the other. Do not read "0 primary hits" as "the sensitivity analysis also found nothing" — it no
longer does, and that gap is the most interesting open thread in this run.
**ID 38354's `local`-space result is the strongest of the 5** — beats all 200/200 of its own matched
controls, non-degenerate sample composition (409/415 cohort samples, 34 ontologies, no single-ontology
dominance), well-behaved regularization (no out-of-support blow-up, unlike its own `long`/`short`
spaces for the same event), and persisted across the GCV→LOOCV+1SE change (q_pooled_z 0.242 → 0.0145).
Survives every internal-consistency check run so far but is **not validated as a real hit** — that was
one event examined after seeing the ranking, not a pre-registered test, and no biological look at what
gene/exon it is has been done. Full write-up:
`.claude/scratch/investigate_pooled_z_candidates_v5_findings.md`.

That combination — a null calibrated in aggregate under both p constructions, no surviving event under
the primary rule, a handful of pooled-z candidates still under investigation, and a fingerprint p
gradient that is clean for SE and noisy for RI — is close to, but not as clean as, a textbook
confirmation of the manuscript's claim that reported epigenetic control of splicing is largely a
cell-type-identity confound. The qualitative conclusion is unchanged from the prior statistic version;
the margin by which it holds is smaller and the pooled-z candidates are unresolved.

**The positive counterpart is cohort-level, not event-level**, and the two do not contradict each other.
Under clean `seqnames`-grouped CV (`splicing_ml`, test AUROC, linear/xgb), sequence features alone
recover nearly the whole model — RI 0.809/0.784 and SE 0.950/0.954, against 0.871/0.855 and 0.957/0.963
for all features — while histone+DNAm alone reach only 0.591/0.587 and 0.641/0.659 over a 0.500 prior
baseline. Epigenetic marks therefore do carry *some* cohort-level signal; what this screen rules out is
that the signal is **locus-specific**. A matched null is blind to regulation shared across loci, so a
diffuse mechanism cancels in the null and reads here as "not locus-specific" — see
`revision/file-changes/09-psi-independent-controls.md` (OUTCOME + RESULT boxes) for the full numbers and
for what the design cannot see.

# 0. Setup and table construction

Loading and derived-table construction only, kept free of analysis so the analytical sections below
read top-to-bottom without side effects. Nothing here produces a plot.

`load-tier1-screen` also sets **`en_available`**, the gate for every Tier-2 chunk. It is deliberately
*data*-driven (are there readable elastic-net metric rows?) rather than file-driven (does a file
exist?), because a cancelled run leaves truncated files and skip-stubs behind, and gating on mere
presence would let the build chunks run and then crash on missing columns.

```{r setup}
library(tidymodels)
library(glmnet)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(pbmcapply)
```

```{r load-session}
# Per-filter (matches 09-1 and everything from 02-2 on): one transcript_filter
# per invocation, chosen by TRANSCRIPT_FILTER (standalone falls back to the
# primary filter).
tf <- Sys.getenv(
  "TRANSCRIPT_FILTER",
  getOption("EpiATLAS_AS_PRIMARY_FILTER", "biotype_filtered")
)

# Load session objects produced by 09-1-ml-local.R (same tf)
sess <- readRDS(sprintf("processed_data/session_09_1_ml_local_%s.rds", tf))
event_dt <- sess$event_dt # trimmed: ID, Event Type, seqnames, Variability, transcript_filter
keep_rows <- sess$keep_rows_manual
rm(sess)
gc()

# `aggregating.rda` is GONE (removed by the per-filter refactor). aggregated_dt
# is per-filter; activeChromHMM (only other object 09-2 needs from that old
# workspace — see the chromhmm-region-annotation chunk below) is now persisted
# directly by 03 (same run as keep_rows_manual, so index-consistent).
aggregated_dt <- fread(
  sprintf("processed_data/aggregated_dt_filtered_%s.csv.gz", tf),
  stringsAsFactors = TRUE
)
activeChromHMM <- readRDS(sprintf("processed_data/activeChromHMM_%s.rds", tf))

# NB: no "restrict to biotype_filtered" subset needed anymore — event_dt (from
# 09-1's session, built off event_annotations_dt_{tf}) and aggregated_dt are
# already scoped to exactly `tf`.
```

```{r load-tier1-screen, cache = TRUE}
event_dir <- file.path("processed_data", "event_models", tf)

plot_dir_ev <- file.path(plot_dir, "event_models", tf)
dir.create(plot_dir_ev, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Helper: aggregate per-event CSVs saved by worker. Robust to (a) no matching
# files and (b) individual unreadable/truncated files (a cancelled/partial run
# can leave a half-written .csv.gz) — pbmclapply otherwise returns error strings
# in place of tables and rbindlist(fill=TRUE) then errors with "Input is
# character…".
#
# When nothing readable is found it returns an empty data.table WITH THE EXPECTED
# COLUMNS for that file type (schema matches 09zz's writers). This is what keeps
# the report renderable at 0 Tier-1 hits AND keeps Positron "Run Above" working:
# knitr chunk options (eval = en_available) are ignored by interactive execution,
# so the EN chunks run regardless; giving them a 0-ROW-but-well-formed table lets
# their `[, := ]` transforms and ggplot() calls no-op on empty data instead of
# crashing on missing columns (e.g. `ID not found`).
.event_csv_schema <- list(
  best_params = c(
    "penalty",
    "mixture",
    ".config",
    "cv_mean_ccc",
    "cv_mean_rmse",
    "cv_mean_rsq_trad",
    "cv_std_err_ccc",
    "cv_std_err_rmse",
    "cv_std_err_rsq_trad",
    "cv_n_ccc",
    "cv_n_rmse",
    "cv_n_rsq_trad",
    "wflow_id",
    "lambda_selection",
    "ID"
  ),
  fit_metrics = c(
    ".metric",
    ".estimator",
    ".estimate",
    "wflow_id",
    "lambda_selection",
    "ID"
  ),
  all_metrics = c(
    "id",
    "penalty",
    "mixture",
    ".metric",
    ".estimator",
    ".estimate",
    ".config",
    "wflow_id",
    "ID"
  ),
  event_summary = c(
    "wflow_id",
    "model_type",
    "n_robust",
    "has_model",
    "expression_bias",
    "lambda_selection",
    "ID"
  ),
  nonzero_coefs = c("wflow_id", "feature", "coef", "lambda_selection", "ID"),
  fold_features = c("wflow_id", "fold", "feature", "lambda_selection", "ID")
)
.event_csv_numeric <- c(
  "penalty",
  "mixture",
  ".estimate",
  "coef",
  "n_robust",
  "cv_mean_ccc",
  "cv_mean_rmse",
  "cv_mean_rsq_trad",
  "cv_std_err_ccc",
  "cv_std_err_rmse",
  "cv_std_err_rsq_trad",
  "cv_n_ccc",
  "cv_n_rmse",
  "cv_n_rsq_trad"
)
.empty_event_dt <- function(pattern) {
  key <- names(.event_csv_schema)[
    vapply(
      names(.event_csv_schema),
      function(k) grepl(k, pattern, fixed = TRUE),
      logical(1)
    )
  ]
  if (length(key) != 1L) {
    return(data.table())
  }
  cols <- .event_csv_schema[[key]]
  data.table::as.data.table(setNames(
    lapply(cols, function(c) {
      if (c %in% .event_csv_numeric) numeric(0) else character(0)
    }),
    cols
  ))
}
read_event_csvs <- function(pattern) {
  files <- list.files(event_dir, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(files) == 0L) {
    return(.empty_event_dt(pattern))
  }
  parts <- pbmclapply(files, function(f) {
    tryCatch(fread(f), error = function(e) NULL)
  })
  parts <- parts[vapply(parts, is.data.frame, logical(1))]
  if (length(parts) == 0L) {
    return(.empty_event_dt(pattern))
  }
  rbindlist(parts, fill = TRUE)
}

# Tier-1 ridge-screen results — significance (is the event epigenetically
# predictable beyond confounds?) is now decided HERE, not by the elastic-net
# rotation test. One row per event PER FEATURE SET (long/short/local): screen_R2/CCC,
# matched feature-rotation null summary, empirical p, effect (= real − null mean),
# and FDR q computed WITHIN each (transcript_filter, Event Type, feature_set) group
# by 09s-aggregate.R. So screen_dt is keyed by (ID, feature_set), NOT by ID alone —
# every join/facet below must carry feature_set or the 3 rows per event collide.
# `sig` is per (event, feature_set); an event is a Tier-2 hit if sig in ANY set.
# The 6 per-event elastic-net tables below are HITS-ONLY (Tier-2), all real PSI.
# Robust load so 09-2 renders on PARTIAL results too (screen still running / not
# yet aggregated). Prefer the aggregated screen_results.csv.gz (real Storey q from
# 09s-aggregate.R over ALL events); if it is absent, assemble a provisional
# screen_dt from whatever per-event screen rows exist and approximate q with BH —
# the final report always uses the true aggregate, this is only so intermediate
# renders don't hard-fail.
.screen_results_file <- file.path(event_dir, "screen_results.csv.gz")
if (file.exists(.screen_results_file)) {
  screen_dt <- fread(.screen_results_file)
} else {
  .screen_rows <- list.files(
    file.path(event_dir, "screen"),
    pattern = "^\\d+_screen\\.csv\\.gz$",
    full.names = TRUE # excludes _screen_null
  )
  if (length(.screen_rows) == 0L) {
    warning(
      "No screen_results.csv.gz and no per-event screen rows — Tier-1 sections ",
      "will be empty. Run the ridge screen (09s) first."
    )
    screen_dt <- data.table(
      ID = integer(),
      feature_set = character(),
      `Event Type` = character(),
      transcript_filter = character(),
      n_samples = integer(),
      R_used = integer(),
      screen_R2 = numeric(),
      screen_CCC = numeric(),
      null_R2_mean = numeric(),
      null_R2_sd = numeric(),
      p_emp = numeric(),
      effect = numeric(),
      note = character()
    )
  } else {
    warning(
      sprintf(
        "screen_results.csv.gz absent — assembling provisional screen_dt from %d ",
        length(.screen_rows)
      ),
      "per-event rows; q via BH proxy (PARTIAL, not the final Storey FDR)."
    )
    screen_dt <- rbindlist(pbmclapply(.screen_rows, fread), fill = TRUE)
    # STAMP GATE. This fallback path is used precisely while a screen is PARTIAL,
    # which is exactly when the directory can hold a mix of statistic versions —
    # so it must filter, unlike the aggregate path (09s-aggregate.R already
    # refuses to mix). Unstamped rows are version 1 (the pre-2026-07-29 leaky
    # statistic). Keep only the newest version present and say what was dropped.
    if (!"stat_version" %in% names(screen_dt)) {
      screen_dt[, stat_version := 1L]
    }
    screen_dt[, stat_version := suppressWarnings(as.integer(stat_version))]
    screen_dt[is.na(stat_version), stat_version := 1L]
    if (uniqueN(screen_dt$stat_version) > 1L) {
      .keep_v <- max(screen_dt$stat_version)
      warning(
        sprintf(
          "per-event screen rows span stat_version %s — keeping only v%d (%d of %d rows)",
          paste(sort(unique(screen_dt$stat_version)), collapse = "/"),
          .keep_v,
          sum(screen_dt$stat_version == .keep_v),
          nrow(screen_dt)
        ),
        immediate. = TRUE
      )
      screen_dt <- screen_dt[stat_version == .keep_v]
    }
  }
  # BH proxy mirrors the aggregator's GROUPED FDR (per tf × Event Type × feature_set),
  # so a provisional render doesn't silently pool the feature sets into one test.
  if (!"feature_set" %in% names(screen_dt)) {
    screen_dt[, feature_set := "long"]
  }
  if (!"transcript_filter" %in% names(screen_dt)) {
    screen_dt[, transcript_filter := tf]
  }
  screen_dt[, q := NA_real_]
  if (nrow(screen_dt) > 0L) {
    if (!"Event Type" %in% names(screen_dt)) {
      screen_dt[event_dt, on = "ID", `Event Type` := `Event Type`]
    }
    screen_dt[
      is.finite(p_emp),
      q := p.adjust(p_emp, method = "BH"),
      by = .(transcript_filter, `Event Type`, feature_set)
    ]
  }
}
screen_dt[, ID := as.integer(ID)]
# Pre-2026-07-29 aggregates are the single omnibus ridge over all epigenetic X —
# that IS the `long` set, so tag rather than drop (keeps old results renderable).
if (!"feature_set" %in% names(screen_dt)) {
  screen_dt[, feature_set := "long"]
}
# Ordered long → short → local (decreasing feature count) for stable facet order.
screen_feature_sets <- intersect(
  c("long", "short", "local"),
  unique(as.character(screen_dt$feature_set))
)
screen_dt[,
  feature_set := factor(
    as.character(feature_set),
    levels = c(
      screen_feature_sets,
      setdiff(unique(as.character(feature_set)), screen_feature_sets)
    )
  )
]
if (!"Event Type" %in% names(screen_dt) && nrow(screen_dt) > 0L) {
  screen_dt[event_dt, on = "ID", `Event Type` := `Event Type`]
}
screen_q_threshold <- 0.1
# Per (event, feature_set) significance. This MUST mirror 09s-aggregate.R's hit rule,
# which is `q < q_threshold` ALONE since 2026-08-01: the one-sided exceedance p already
# encodes direction, so the former `& effect > 0` clause was redundant, and on the raw
# statistic it was outlier-dominated (it passed ~3/4 of events for numerical reasons —
# see QC check 5). The aggregator's `EpiATLAS_AS_SCREEN_MIN_EFFECT` survives as an
# opt-in variance-collapse filter acting on `effect_bounded`, and defaults to no filter.
screen_dt[,
  sig := is.finite(q) & q < screen_q_threshold
]
# … and the per-EVENT roll-up (sig in ANY feature set) — this is what defines a
# Tier-2 hit in 09s-aggregate.R, and what the biology sections downstream split on.
screen_dt[, sig_any := any(sig %in% TRUE), by = ID]
screen_sig_ids <- sort(unique(screen_dt[sig %in% TRUE, ID]))

# en_available — is there USABLE Tier-2/EN data? Gates every EN-dependent chunk
# (via `eval = en_available`) so the Tier-1 (screen) report always renders, even
# at 0 hits or on a partial run. DATA-driven, not just file-presence: read the
# all_metrics (CV-metrics) tables robustly and require ≥1 row with a real metric
# column. This is deliberately stricter than "a file exists" — a run can leave
# only truncated files or skip-stubs (`data.table(ID=…)` with no `.metric`), and
# gating on mere presence would then let build-cv-tables run and crash on the
# missing ID/.metric columns.
.en_all_metrics <- read_event_csvs("^\\d+_all_metrics\\.csv\\.gz$")
en_available <- nrow(.en_all_metrics) > 0L &&
  ".metric" %in% names(.en_all_metrics)
```

# 1. Tier 1 — the ridge screen: is any event predictable beyond its matched null?

This section decides significance for **every** event; nothing downstream can add an event the screen
did not select. `09s-ridge-screen.R` computes, per event and per feature space, a closed-form
group-leave-one-ontology-out ridge **partial-R²** — the variance in PSI explained by epigenetics *after*
protocol, gene expression and TSS distance are absorbed as unpenalised confounds — then re-computes that
same statistic on **matched control loci** — same event type, same variability tier, different
chromosome — while keeping this event's PSI. `screen_rotations` is per-Event-Type: **818 for RI**
(its full eligible pool) and **200 for SE**. That gives an empirical p, and `09s-aggregate.R` turns the
p-values into FDR **q** within each (`transcript_filter`, `Event Type`, `feature_set`) group.

**An event is significant when `q < threshold`** — that single condition, nothing else. The one-sided
exceedance p already encodes *direction* (it is the mass of the null at or above the real R²), so the
`effect > 0` clause this rule used to carry was redundant; it was also actively misleading on the raw
statistic, where `effect = real R² − mean(null R²)` is mean-based and passed ~3/4 of events for purely
numerical reasons (§1.1 check 5). Dropped 2026-08-01; see `09s-aggregate.R`.

### The order of this section is the argument

The QC/calibration chunk comes **first, on purpose**. A hit list from a miscalibrated null is
meaningless, so the null is audited before any result is read:

1. **`screen-diagnostics`** — is the null honest, is the fingerprint pattern present, is the
   negative-R² tail explained?
2. **`screen-significance-plots`** — the actual per-group results and hit counts.
3. **`screen-floor-sensitivity`** — could the test have rejected anything at all? The p-floor
   arithmetic and the floor-free pooled-z sensitivity p (§1.3).
4. **`screen-null-histograms`** — the raw material: where each real R² falls inside its own null.

### Hypotheses this section discriminates between

- **H1 — genuine event-specific epigenetic control.** Some events' local chromatin predicts their PSI
  better than unrelated loci do. *Signature:* an excess of events in the leftmost p bin over uniform,
  and survival after FDR.
- **H2 — cell-type fingerprint only.** All apparent predictability is shared cell-type identity.
  *Signature:* flat p histogram and no survivors after FDR, with p never approaching significance even
  in the highest raw-R² stratum. High-R² events are the clearest fingerprint cases, not the best hits.
  (Read this off `median_p` per R² stratum, **not** off `effect` — see check 5.)
- **H3 — broken/optimistic null** (a nuisance hypothesis that must be excluded before H1 or H2 can be
  read). *Signature:* p piling up toward 0 monotonically across all bins. Note that an implausibly
  large fraction of `effect > 0` indicates a corrupted `effect`, not an optimistic null — check 5.

H2 vs H1 is the manuscript's central question; H3 is why the diagnostics run first.

## 1.1 Screen QC: is the null honest? (read this before the results)

Five checks, each with an expected shape and a specific failure mode:

**(1) Null calibration — empirical-p distribution, per (Event Type x feature set).**
*Expected under no genome-wide signal:* flat (uniform), because a matched control locus should beat the
real locus about as often as chance dictates.
*Expected under genuine signal:* flat, **plus** a bump in the leftmost bin — the hits.
*Failure:* a monotone pile-up toward 0 across all bins means the null is systematically too weak
(controls handicapped somehow — e.g. mismatched sample sets or fewer usable features), and **no hit list
from this run can be trusted**. Checked per **family** — `(Event Type, feature_set)`, the unit the FDR is actually computed in — not
per feature set alone. SE outnumbers RI ~18:1, so a pooled panel is an SE panel and an RI-specific
failure would be invisible in it; the two types' nulls are also measurably different (KS p = 0.0072 on
their standardised null z). Every table and panel in this subsection is grouped that way.

**(2) Fingerprint check — `effect` and p within raw-R² strata.**
*Hypothesis:* if predictability were event-specific, the best-predicted events would also be the ones
that most beat their null, so `effect` should rise with raw R².
*Fingerprint prediction (H2):* the top stratum still fails to reject — median p well above the FDR
threshold and no survivor after BH — even though it holds the best-predicted events in the genome.
**Read that off `median_p`, not off `effect`.** On the completed screen `effect` is positive in
**80–100%** of events in every stratum above the `<=0` baseline, in every family, with exactly one
exception: RI/short's top (`> 0.5`) bucket holds a single event with a negative effect — illustrating
how noisy a 1-event stratum is, not a reversal of the pattern. Its *magnitude* is unstable across
strata (from near 0 to several tens), which is check 5's corruption signature, not evidence for H1: raw
`effect` is mean-based and the R² blow-ups drag it. `median_p` behaves better: it falls cleanly with R²
in the two large families, SE/local (0.716 → 0.030) and SE/long (0.522 → 0.127), and the `> 0.5`
stratum never approaches significance in any family (family min q 0.551–0.842).
*Deduction from that pattern:* raw R² is measuring cell-type identity, and any published ranking of
"most epigenetically predictable events" built on R² alone is a ranking of fingerprint strength.

**(3) Negative-R² tail vs sample size.**
Group-LOO R² can go sharply negative; the question is whether that is a bug or expected instability.
*Expected:* the negative tail concentrates in **small-n** events, where holding out a whole ontology
group removes a large share of the data. It should also shrink from `long` → `local` as the p ≫ n
pressure eases.
*Deduction if very negative R² appears at large n, or does not ease as features are dropped:* suspect a
data or confound-partition problem rather than small-sample noise.

**(4) Silently voided events (`stat_version` ≥ 2 only).** The leak-fixed statistic fits the confound design
per fold on training rows, but its constant-column guard is evaluated over *all* rows — so a fold whose
training subset makes a confound constant yields a rank-deficient design, an `NA` out-of-fold residual, and
an `NA` R² for the whole event. `screen_CCC` does **not** fail with it: `.ccc()` filters non-finite pairs
and returns a value computed on the survivors, which looks valid.
*Signature:* `screen_R2` NA with a **finite** `screen_CCC`, `R_used == 0`, and no `note`.
*Expected:* a small percentage, concentrated at low `n_samples`.
*Deduction:* those events are **excluded, not tested** — so they cannot produce false positives, but the
loss is non-random (it hits exactly the low-*n* stratum check 3 examines), and any `screen_CCC` reported for
them is computed on an unknown subset and must not be quoted.

**(5) Is `effect` still a usable effect size?** `effect = screen_R2 − mean(null_R2)` is **mean**-based, so a
single exploded null value corrupts it; `p_emp` is **rank**-based and does not care.
*Expected if healthy:* the fraction with `effect > 0` is broadly consistent with the fraction at small
`p_emp`, and median `effect` does not flip sign across `|screen_R2|` strata.
Note that `effect > 0` at ~50% alongside `p_emp ≤ 0.05` at ~5% is **healthy**, not contradictory —
`effect` is a symmetric difference, so half of it is positive under the null. The pathology is `effect > 0`
drifting far from 50% (**79.3%** on the completed screen) *together with* a material fraction of
`|screen_R2| > 1` (**50.1%** — over half of all rows, up from 29.6% under the prior GCV λ selection;
the LOOCV+1SE change made this worse, not better, and that is not yet explained), which means the
null mean is being dragged by exploded out-of-fold predictions.
*Deduction if that happens:* `effect` has stopped carrying information about direction and is positive for
numerical reasons — which is why it is no longer part of the hit rule at all. Use `q` alone for inference,
treat raw `effect` as unreportable (`effect_bounded` / `effect_ccc` are the bounded substitutes), and see
`revision/file-changes/09-event-models-redesign.md` TODO-2.

```{r screen-diagnostics}
sd_fin <- screen_dt[is.finite(p_emp) & is.finite(screen_R2) & is.finite(effect)]
sd_fin[event_dt, Variability := `Variability`, on = "ID"]

# EVERY diagnostic below is grouped by (Event Type x feature_set) — the FDR family,
# NOT feature_set alone.
#
# This matters more than it looks. SE outnumbers RI ~18:1 (32,368 vs 1,776 events),
# so anything pooled across event types is an SE diagnostic with RI invisible: RI's
# null could be badly miscalibrated and the pooled p-histogram would still look
# flat. And the two event types demonstrably differ — a KS test on their
# leave-one-out standardised null z gives p = 0.0072, with q99.99 of 9.73 (SE) vs
# 5.93 (RI). This is the same trap that made a pooled-z reference read as calibrated
# at ratio 1.01 while actually being 1.43x anti-conservative for SE and 0.41x
# conservative for RI: majority-class dominance hiding a minority-class failure.
# Diagnose in the unit the inference is done in.
.diag_by <- c("Event Type", "feature_set")

# Coverage per family: rotations used, n_features (the point of the split), and
# degenerate-event notes (NA = fit fine).
cat("Screen coverage per Event Type x feature set:\n")
# NB every summary must have a TYPE-STABLE result across groups: median() on an
# integer column returns integer for odd-length groups but double for even-length
# ones, which makes data.table abort with "Column N ... is type 'double' but
# expecting type 'integer'" as soon as the groups differ in parity. Hence the
# explicit as.double()/as.integer() casts — do not drop them.
print(screen_dt[,
  .(
    n_events = .N,
    finite_p = sum(is.finite(p_emp)),
    median_features = as.double(median(n_features, na.rm = TRUE)),
    R_used_median = as.double(median(R_used, na.rm = TRUE)),
    R_used_below_max = sum(R_used < max(R_used, na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  by = .diag_by
][order(`Event Type`, feature_set)])
cat("Degenerate-event notes (NA = screened cleanly):\n")
print(screen_dt[, .N, by = c(.diag_by, "note")][order(
  `Event Type`,
  feature_set,
  -N
)])

# (1) NULL CALIBRATION — p_emp should be ~flat under the null. A broken/optimistic
# null piles p toward 0 across all bins; genuine signal shows only as a modest
# excess in the leftmost bin over the uniform (dashed) line.
# Calibration must be checked PER FAMILY (Event Type x feature set) — each is its
# own set of tests with its own FDR, so one family's null can be broken while
# another's is fine, and a pooled panel would hide it (see .diag_by above).
n_bins <- 100L
.unif_dt <- sd_fin[, .(y = .N / n_bins), by = .diag_by]
print(
  ggplot(sd_fin, aes(x = p_emp)) +
    geom_histogram(
      breaks = seq(0, 1, 1 / n_bins),
      fill = "grey70",
      color = "white"
    ) +
    geom_hline(
      data = .unif_dt,
      aes(yintercept = y),
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "firebrick"
    ) +
    facet_grid(
      factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze) + Variability ~ feature_set,
      scales = "free_y"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      title = "Tier-1 null calibration: empirical p per Event Type x feature set",
      x = "Empirical p (matched feature-rotation null)",
      y = "Number of events",
      caption = paste(
        "Dashed = uniform expectation (per panel). Flat = well-calibrated null; excess",
        "in the leftmost bin = genome-wide signal; a monotone pile-up toward 0 would",
        "indicate an optimistic (broken) null. Read RI on its own: it is ~5% of events,",
        "so pooling it with SE would hide an RI-specific failure entirely."
      )
    )
)
ggsave(
  file.path(plot_dir_ev, "screen_pvalue_calibration.pdf"),
  width = 3 + 3 * max(1L, uniqueN(sd_fin$`Event Type`)),
  height = 2 + 2.2 * max(1L, uniqueN(sd_fin$feature_set)),
  limitsize = FALSE
)

# (2) FINGERPRINT — effect & p within raw-R2 strata. High raw R2 with effect ≈ 0
# and non-small p = cell-type fingerprint, not event-specific signal (binned
# complement to screen_effect_vs_r2.pdf). READ THE `median_p` COLUMN, not the effect
# columns: on the real screen `effect` is outlier-corrupted (check 5 below), so the
# "effect ≈ 0" half of that signature is not observable and `median_p` carries the
# argument on its own. NB the cut here is on SIGNED screen_R2 (0/0.1/0.2/0.5), which is
# NOT check 5's abs(screen_R2) magnitude cut — the two give opposite-looking p gradients
# and must not be compared to each other.
sd_fin[,
  r2_stratum := cut(
    screen_R2,
    c(-Inf, 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, Inf),
    labels = c("<=0", "(0,0.1]", "(0.1,0.2]", "(0.2,0.5]", ">0.5")
  )
]
cat(
  "Fingerprint check — effect & p within raw-R2 strata, per Event Type x feature set:\n"
)
print(sd_fin[,
  .(
    n = .N,
    median_R2 = round(median(screen_R2), 3),
    median_effect = round(median(effect), 4),
    pct_effect_pos = round(100 * mean(effect > 0), 1),
    median_p = round(median(p_emp), 3)
  ),
  by = c(.diag_by, "r2_stratum")
][order(`Event Type`, feature_set, r2_stratum)])

# (3) SMALL-n INSTABILITY — very-negative group-LOO R2 concentrates in small
# events (expected), not a bug. y clipped at the 1st percentile for readability.
print(
  ggplot(sd_fin, aes(x = n_samples, y = screen_R2, color = sig)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
    geom_point(alpha = .3, size = .7) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(`TRUE` = "firebrick", `FALSE` = "grey60"),
      labels = c(`TRUE` = "significant", `FALSE` = "not sig"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(
      ylim = c(quantile(sd_fin$screen_R2, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
    ) +
    facet_grid(feature_set ~ `Event Type`) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      title = "Screen R2 vs sample size (very-negative R2 = small-n LOO instability)",
      x = "n samples (event)",
      y = "Group-LOO screen R2",
      caption = paste(
        "Per feature set: the p >> n regime eases as features are dropped, so the",
        "negative-R2 tail should shrink from long -> short -> local."
      )
    )
)
ggsave(
  file.path(plot_dir_ev, "screen_r2_vs_nsamples.pdf"),
  width = 3 + 3 * max(1L, uniqueN(sd_fin$`Event Type`)),
  height = 2 + 2.2 * max(1L, uniqueN(sd_fin$feature_set)),
  limitsize = FALSE
)

# (4) SILENTLY VOIDED EVENTS. See revision/file-changes/09-event-models-redesign.md
# TODO-1. A fold whose train rows make a confound constant gives a rank-deficient
# design -> NA out-of-fold residual -> NA screen_R2 for the WHOLE event, while
# .ccc() filters non-finite pairs and still returns a value. So the signature of the
# defect is: screen_R2 NA, screen_CCC FINITE, R_used == 0, note absent.
cat("\n=== (4) event losses and their attribution ===\n")
screen_dt[, `:=`(
  .r2_na = !is.finite(screen_R2),
  .ccc_ok = is.finite(screen_CCC)
)]
loss_tab <- screen_dt[,
  .(
    n_rows = .N,
    finite_p = sum(is.finite(p_emp)),
    pct_finite_p = round(100 * mean(is.finite(p_emp)), 2),
    voided_silently = sum(.r2_na & .ccc_ok), # R2 NA but CCC finite = the defect
    voided_both = sum(.r2_na & !.ccc_ok),
    with_note = sum(!is.na(note))
  ),
  by = .diag_by
][order(`Event Type`, feature_set)]
print(loss_tab)
if (sum(loss_tab$voided_silently) > 0L) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "!! %d row(s) have screen_R2 = NA with a FINITE screen_CCC and no note.\n   Those events were EXCLUDED, not tested; their screen_CCC is computed on an\n   unknown subset of samples and must not be quoted. n_samples of affected rows:\n",
    sum(loss_tab$voided_silently)
  ))
  print(summary(screen_dt[.r2_na & .ccc_ok, n_samples]))
  cat("   (a low-n concentration is the expected signature; see TODO-1)\n")
}
cat("Degenerate `note` values actually recorded:\n")
print(screen_dt[!is.na(note), .N, by = note][order(-N)])

# (5) IS `effect` STILL A USABLE EFFECT SIZE? See TODO-2. `effect` is mean-based
# (screen_R2 - mean(null_R2)) so one exploded null corrupts it; p_emp is rank-based
# and immune. When the out-of-fold R2 blows up, `effect > 0` stops carrying
# information — it holds for most events for numerical reasons. This is why the hit
# rule no longer uses it (dropped 2026-08-01); the check stays, as a health signal.
cat(
  "\n=== (5) numeric health of screen_R2, and whether `effect` still means anything ===\n"
)
mag <- rbindlist(lapply(c(1, 10, 100, 1000), function(t) {
  data.table(
    threshold = t,
    n_rows = sum(abs(sd_fin$screen_R2) > t),
    pct = round(100 * mean(abs(sd_fin$screen_R2) > t), 2)
  )
}))
cat(
  "Rows with |screen_R2| above each threshold (an honest out-of-fold R2 should sit\nnear or below 1; large values are prediction blow-ups, not signal):\n"
)
print(mag)
sd_fin[, .blow := abs(screen_R2) > 10]
cat(
  "\nDo blow-ups track sample size / lambda? (small n + small lambda = the known cause)\n"
)
print(sd_fin[,
  .(
    n_rows = .N,
    median_n_samples = as.double(median(n_samples, na.rm = TRUE)),
    median_lambda = signif(median(lambda, na.rm = TRUE), 3)
  ),
  by = .blow
][order(.blow)])
.pct_eff_pos <- 100 * mean(sd_fin$effect > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
.pct_p_small <- 100 * mean(sd_fin$p_emp <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf(
  "\neffect > 0: %.1f%% of rows | p_emp <= 0.05: %.2f%%\n",
  .pct_eff_pos,
  .pct_p_small
))
sd_fin[,
  .r2_mag := cut(
    abs(screen_R2),
    c(-Inf, 1, 10, 100, Inf),
    labels = c("<=1", "(1,10]", "(10,100]", ">100")
  )
]
print(sd_fin[,
  .(
    n = .N,
    median_effect = signif(median(effect), 3),
    median_null_mean = signif(median(null_R2_mean), 3),
    pct_effect_pos = round(100 * mean(effect > 0), 1),
    median_p = round(median(p_emp), 3)
  ),
  by = .r2_mag
][order(.r2_mag)])
# Trigger on the RIGHT signature. Under a well-behaved null, `effect > 0` sits near
# 50% (it is a symmetric difference) while p_emp <= 0.05 sits near 5% — those two are
# consistent, so their ratio is NOT evidence of anything. The pathology is `effect > 0`
# drifting far from 50% (the null MEAN being dragged by exploded values) together with
# a material blow-up fraction.
.blow_pct <- 100 * mean(abs(sd_fin$screen_R2) > 1, na.rm = TRUE)
.eff_skew <- abs(.pct_eff_pos - 50)
if (.blow_pct > 5 || .eff_skew > 15) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "!! %.1f%% of rows have |screen_R2| > 1 and `effect > 0` holds for %.1f%% (expected\n   ~50%% under a symmetric null). `effect` is outlier-corrupted and is NOT a usable\n   effect size here -- which is why it is no longer part of the hit rule at all (the\n   `effect > 0` clause was dropped 2026-08-01). Use q alone for inference; do not quote\n   `effect` or mean(screen_R2); `effect_bounded`/`effect_ccc` are the bounded\n   substitutes. See revision/file-changes/09-event-models-redesign.md TODO-2.\n",
    .blow_pct,
    .pct_eff_pos
  ))
} else {
  cat(sprintf(
    "effect looks usable: %.1f%% of rows |screen_R2| > 1, `effect > 0` at %.1f%% (~50%%\nexpected under a symmetric null).\n",
    .blow_pct,
    .pct_eff_pos
  ))
}
# p_emp is rank-based, so it should survive the blow-ups — verify, since the whole
# FDR rests on it.
.pmin <- min(sd_fin$p_emp, na.rm = TRUE)
.rmax <- max(sd_fin$R_used, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf(
  "\nmin p_emp = %.6g; expected floor 1/(R_used+1) = %.6g -> %s\n",
  .pmin,
  1 / (.rmax + 1),
  if (abs(.pmin - 1 / (.rmax + 1)) < 1e-9) "OK" else "UNEXPECTED, investigate"
))
screen_dt[, c(".r2_na", ".ccc_ok") := NULL]
sd_fin[, c(".blow", ".r2_mag") := NULL]
```

## 1.2 Screen results: hit counts, p-values, and fingerprint unmasking

Only read this once section 1.1 has established the null is calibrated.

**Per-group counts.** Reported by `(Event Type, feature_set)` — the exact grouping the FDR was computed
within, so these *are* the per-family hit counts. The roll-up table beside it gives `n_sig_any_set`
(the Tier-2 hit definition) and `n_sig_all_sets`. Because the spaces are nested, expect
`n_sig_all_sets ≤ n_sig_any_set` and expect the two to be *close* if signal is broad, far apart if
signal is space-specific.

**Plot 2 — empirical p per event.** Same calibration logic as §1.1, now split by event type as well, so
a signal restricted to one event type is visible. SE and RI differ in sample size and in baseline
predictability, so their p distributions should be read separately rather than pooled.

**Plot 3 — `effect` vs raw R²: the fingerprint unmasking.** The single most important plot in the
report.
*Expected under H2 (fingerprint):* a horizontal band at `effect ≈ 0` that extends all the way to the
highest R², with significant points absent or scattered.
*Expected under H1 (real signal):* points lifting off the `effect = 0` line, and — importantly — the
lift-off need **not** be at high R². Genuine event-specific signal is expected at *modest* R² with a
clearly-beaten null, precisely because it is not riding the cell-type axis.
*Read this plot with check 5 in hand.* On the completed screen neither expectation is legible, because
the y-axis quantity is corrupted: raw `effect` is mean-based, 79.3% of rows are positive against ~50%
under a symmetric null, and the clipping to `|R²|, |effect| ≤ 1` now drops **over half** of all rows
(the panel's printed count gives the exact figure for this run — check it, since the blow-up rate moved
from 29.6% to 50.1% between statistic versions and this clip fraction moves with it). So the panel
shows where the surviving points sit, not whether anything lifted off.
*Deduction:* **`q` identifies a hit, not `effect`** — `effect` left the hit rule on 2026-08-01. Use this
plot as a shape diagnostic and §1.2's hit table plus §1.3's floor arithmetic as the verdict; if a bounded
version of the vertical axis is wanted, `effect_bounded` / `effect_ccc` exist for it.

**Plot 4 (new) — does narrowing the feature space recover diluted signal?** Per event, `effect` in the
narrower space vs `effect` in `long`, with the identity line drawn.
*Hypothesis being tested:* the omnibus `long` ridge dilutes exon-local signal across hundreds of far
chromHMM windows, so genuinely local signal should sit **above** the identity line.
*Deduction if a substantial fraction lies above the line:* the per-feature-set split is doing real work
and a single omnibus screen under-reports; the accompanying `median_delta` / `pct_improved` table
quantifies it. **Caveat, same as Plot 3:** these are differences of the *raw* `effect`, so they inherit
its outlier corruption and 63% of the points fall outside the clip window. On the completed screen the
narrower spaces do sit above the line (`pct_improved` 61–85%), but no family gained a single hit from it
— so read this as "the split changes the statistic", not "the split recovers signal".
*Deduction if points cluster on the line:* the far chromHMM windows were contributing neither signal nor
meaningful dilution, and the three spaces are largely redundant for significance purposes.

```{r screen-significance-plots}
# Screen significance plots — built DIRECTLY from screen_dt (one row per event),
# so they always render, even at 0 hits / on a partial run (independent of the EN
# tables). Previously these were computed off emp_p_dt, which broadcasts screen
# values across the EN (feature_set × lambda) rows and is therefore empty when
# there are no hits.
screen_plot_dt <- screen_dt[, .(
  ID,
  feature_set,
  emp_p = p_emp,
  q,
  effect,
  screen_R2,
  sig
)]
screen_plot_dt[event_dt, on = "ID", `Event Type` := `Event Type`]
screen_plot_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]
.n_fs <- max(1L, uniqueN(screen_plot_dt$feature_set))

# Significance summary per (Event Type × feature_set) — the exact grouping the FDR
# was computed within, so these counts are the per-group hit counts.
print(screen_plot_dt[,
  .(
    n_sig = sum(sig, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_total = sum(!is.na(q)),
    pct_sig = round(100 * mean(sig, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  ),
  by = .(`Event Type`, feature_set)
][order(`Event Type`, feature_set)])

# Roll-up: an event counts as a hit if significant in ANY feature set (Tier-2's
# definition). Reported alongside the per-set counts because the sets are nested
# (local ⊂ short ⊂ long), so per-set counts are not independent and don't add up.
print(screen_plot_dt[,
  .(n_sig_sets = sum(sig, na.rm = TRUE)),
  by = .(`Event Type`, ID)
][,
  .(
    n_events = uniqueN(ID),
    n_sig_any_set = uniqueN(ID[n_sig_sets > 0L]),
    n_sig_all_sets = uniqueN(ID[n_sig_sets == .n_fs])
  ),
  by = `Event Type`
][order(`Event Type`)])

# Plot 2: screen empirical-p per event, event type × feature set.
print(
  ggplot(
    screen_plot_dt[is.finite(emp_p)],
    aes(x = emp_p, fill = `Event Type`)
  ) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 100, alpha = .7, position = "identity") +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = screen_q_threshold,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "red"
    ) +
    facet_grid(`Event Type` ~ feature_set, scales = "free_y") +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      title = "Tier-1 ridge-screen empirical p-value (per event, per feature set)",
      x = "Empirical p (matched feature-rotation null)",
      y = "Number of events",
      caption = paste(
        "Rows = feature set (long = all epigenetic; short = drop far chromHMM;",
        "local = drop all chromHMM). FDR is computed within each row × column cell.",
        "Significant = q < threshold AND effect (real - mean null R2) > 0."
      )
    )
)
ggsave(
  file.path(plot_dir_ev, "screen_pvalue.pdf"),
  width = 10,
  height = 2 + 2.2 * .n_fs,
  limitsize = FALSE
)

# Plot 3: effect vs raw R² — the fingerprint unmasking. High raw R² with effect
# ≈ 0 = cell-type fingerprint (a random locus predicts as well). Colour is the real
# hit rule, q < threshold alone — `effect` is diagnostic here, not a criterion.
# CLIPPED, deliberately. `effect = screen_R2 - mean(null_R2)`, so while the v2
# out-of-fold R2 blows up (see QC check 5) the y-axis is dominated by its own x-axis:
# cor(effect, screen_R2) measured 0.988 across all rows vs -0.05 restricted to
# |R2| <= 1. Unclipped, this panel is one dot plus a diagonal streak and shows NO
# fingerprint structure. The excluded count is printed, not hidden.
.p3 <- screen_plot_dt[is.finite(effect) & is.finite(screen_R2)]
.p3_lim <- 1
.p3_out <- .p3[abs(screen_R2) > .p3_lim | abs(effect) > .p3_lim, .N]
cat(sprintf(
  "Plot 3 clipped to |R2| and |effect| <= %g: %d of %d rows (%.1f%%) outside, not drawn.\n",
  .p3_lim,
  .p3_out,
  nrow(.p3),
  100 * .p3_out / max(1L, nrow(.p3))
))
print(
  ggplot(.p3, aes(x = screen_R2, y = effect, color = sig)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
    geom_point(alpha = .4, size = .8) +
    coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(-.p3_lim, .p3_lim),
      ylim = c(-.p3_lim, .p3_lim)
    ) +
    facet_grid(`Event Type` ~ feature_set, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "firebrick", `FALSE` = "grey60")) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      title = "Screen effect (real - null) vs raw R2: fingerprint unmasking",
      x = "Raw group-LOO screen R2",
      y = "Effect = real R2 - mean null R2",
      color = "Significant\n(q < threshold)",
      caption = paste(
        "High raw R2 with effect near 0 = cell-type fingerprint (random control",
        "loci predict as well). CLIPPED axes -- see the printed count of excluded",
        "rows. While the out-of-fold R2 blows up, `effect` is outlier-corrupted and",
        "is NOT comparable across rows; read q, not effect. See TODO-2 in",
        "revision/file-changes/09-event-models-redesign.md."
      )
    )
)
ggsave(
  file.path(plot_dir_ev, "screen_effect_vs_r2.pdf"),
  width = 10,
  height = 2 + 2.2 * .n_fs,
  limitsize = FALSE
)

# Does narrowing the feature space actually recover diluted local signal? Per event,
# compare effect across sets — the motivation for splitting the screen at all. A
# positive local-minus-long effect means the omnibus ridge was diluting that event.
if (.n_fs > 1L) {
  eff_wide <- dcast(
    screen_plot_dt[is.finite(effect)],
    ID + `Event Type` ~ feature_set,
    value.var = "effect"
  )
  .pairs <- intersect(c("short", "local"), names(eff_wide))
  if ("long" %in% names(eff_wide) && length(.pairs) > 0L) {
    eff_delta <- melt(
      eff_wide,
      id.vars = c("ID", "Event Type", "long"),
      measure.vars = .pairs,
      variable.name = "feature_set",
      value.name = "effect"
    )[is.finite(effect) & is.finite(long)]
    eff_delta[, delta := effect - long]
    cat("Effect gain from narrowing the feature space (vs `long`):\n")
    print(eff_delta[,
      .(
        n = .N,
        median_delta = round(median(delta), 4),
        pct_improved = round(100 * mean(delta > 0), 1)
      ),
      by = .(`Event Type`, feature_set)
    ][order(`Event Type`, feature_set)])

    .ed_lim <- 1
    .ed_out <- eff_delta[abs(long) > .ed_lim | abs(effect) > .ed_lim, .N]
    cat(sprintf(
      "Clipped to |effect| <= %g on both axes: %d of %d points (%.1f%%) not drawn.\n",
      .ed_lim,
      .ed_out,
      nrow(eff_delta),
      100 * .ed_out / max(1L, nrow(eff_delta))
    ))
    print(
      ggplot(eff_delta, aes(x = long, y = effect, color = `Event Type`)) +
        coord_cartesian(
          xlim = c(-.ed_lim, .ed_lim),
          ylim = c(-.ed_lim, .ed_lim)
        ) +
        geom_abline(
          slope = 1,
          intercept = 0,
          linetype = "dashed",
          color = "grey40"
        ) +
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey60") +
        geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey60") +
        geom_point(alpha = .3, size = .7) +
        facet_grid(feature_set ~ `Event Type`) +
        theme_bw() +
        labs(
          title = "Does a narrower feature space recover diluted local signal?",
          x = "Effect in `long` (all epigenetic features)",
          y = "Effect in the narrower feature set",
          caption = paste(
            "Dashed = equality; points above it = the narrower space beats the omnibus",
            "ridge. NB the dilution rationale predicts local >= short >= long, but the",
            "measured ordering is short > long > local (local is the only set that gets",
            "WORSE), which argues against dilution as the mechanism. Axes clipped; see",
            "the printed excluded count, and TODO-2 on effect being outlier-corrupted."
          )
        )
    )
    ggsave(
      file.path(plot_dir_ev, "screen_effect_by_feature_set.pdf"),
      width = 10,
      height = 2 + 2.2 * length(.pairs),
      limitsize = FALSE
    )
  }
}
```

## 1.3 Could the test have found anything? The p-floor and the floor-free sensitivity p

The exceedance p cannot go below **`1/(R_used + 1)`** — 0.00498 at SE's 200 rotations, 0.00122 at RI's
818. BH at `q < threshold` only passes a p-value at rank *k* if `p ≤ k·q/m`. Those two facts can conflict:
if a family's floor sits *above* what BH allows, **no event in it can pass FDR regardless of how strong
its signal is**, and a 0-hit result there says nothing on its own. On the completed screen that is the
situation in **every one of the six families** (`floor_can_pass = FALSE` throughout): SE needed ≥ 1,608
events tied at the floor and has 191 / 208 / 199 (long / short / local), RI needed ≥ 22 and has
2 / 2 / 2 — the same count in every one of RI's three feature spaces, unlike the earlier statistic
version where RI's counts differed sharply across spaces (0 / 3 / 1). Whether that is the same 2 events
recurring in all three spaces or 2 different events per space has not been checked.

This is a distinct nuisance hypothesis from the three in §1, and it must be excluded before the negative
result can be read:

> **H4 — the test lacked the resolution to reject anything.** *Signature:* every candidate event tied at
> exactly `1/(R_used + 1)`, and `floor_can_pass = FALSE` in the table below. A flat p-histogram does
> **not** exclude H4 — it only excludes a broken null (H3).

Raising the rotation count cannot fix it, and the reason is **not** simply that the pool is too small —
SE's matched pool runs to ~15,000 loci. `k_at_floor` counts events that beat **every** one of their `R`
controls, so a larger pool is a *higher* bar: if an event sits at quantile *u* among its controls,
P(beat all R) ≈ *u*^R decays geometrically, while the BH requirement `p_floor·m/q` eases only like 1/R.
Measured across this project's own rotation counts (under the prior, `stat_version` 4 statistic), the
requirement eased 9× (198.5 → 22) while RI/local's `k_at_floor` fell 25× (25 → 1) — the gap got ~3×
worse. Under the current `stat_version` 5 statistic at the same R = 818, RI/local's `k_at_floor` is 2,
not 1 — the λ-selection change moved this specific count, though the conclusion it supports (RI's ~818
control ceiling is far below what its k needs) is unaffected either way. RI is additionally capped: its
~818 eligible controls are set by the RI event count itself, so no rotation setting reaches the
thousands its measured *k* would need. Dropping low-variance events does not help either (the BH
threshold `k·q/m` is scale-invariant, since *k* shrinks with *m*). What does fix it is a second,
**floor-free** p-value: standardise each event's statistic by its own matched null
(`z = (R² − mean null)/sd null`) and read the p off a reference of leave-one-out-standardised **null** z
values pooled **within the FDR family** `(transcript_filter, Event Type, feature_set)`. Only the
dimensionless deviation *shape* is borrowed — each event's own R² level and scale stay local, so a
cell-type-fingerprint event (high null **mean**) still gets a small z and is not rescued by this.

The family stratification is not cosmetic: pooling across Event Types measures as 1.43× anti-conservative
for SE and 0.41× conservative for RI (α = 10⁻⁴), errors that cancel to a deceptive 1.01 when averaged over
a 95%-SE sample. Within-family it is 1.00 (SE) / 0.91–1.05 (RI). A median/MAD scale is 2.6–5.2×
anti-conservative and must not be substituted.

**This is a sensitivity analysis, not the primary result.** `sig` and the Tier-2 hit list stay on the
exceedance p, which assumes only that an event's own controls are exchangeable with it; the pooled-z p
additionally assumes a family-common deviation shape. Two independent constructions agreeing is the
claim; the pooled-z alone is the weaker of the two.

*Deduction if both give 0 hits (the current state):* the negative result is not an artifact of resolution —
it survives a construction with ~4 orders more of it.
*Deduction if pooled-z yields hits where the exceedance p could not:* those are candidates the floor was
hiding, but they inherit the extra assumption, so check the calibration ratio for that family and the
effect-size guard below before treating any as real.

```{r screen-floor-sensitivity}
# (a) p-FLOOR ARITHMETIC per FDR family -- can the primary statistic pass at all?
screen_min_effect <- getOption("EpiATLAS_AS_SCREEN_MIN_EFFECT", 0)
.has_tf <- "transcript_filter" %in% names(screen_dt)
.by <- if (.has_tf) {
  c("transcript_filter", "Event Type", "feature_set")
} else {
  c("Event Type", "feature_set")
}
floor_tab <- screen_dt[
  is.finite(p_emp),
  {
    m <- .N
    fl <- 1 / (max(R_used, na.rm = TRUE) + 1)
    k <- sum(p_emp <= fl + 1e-12 & effect > screen_min_effect, na.rm = TRUE)
    .(
      m_tests = m,
      p_floor = signif(fl, 3),
      k_at_floor = k,
      bh_allows = if (k > 0L) {
        signif(k * screen_q_threshold / m, 3)
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      floor_can_pass = k > 0L && fl <= k * screen_q_threshold / m,
      k_needed = ceiling(fl * m / screen_q_threshold)
    )
  },
  by = .by
]
cat("Can the primary (exceedance) p clear FDR in each family?\n")
print(floor_tab[order(`Event Type`, feature_set)])
if (any(!floor_tab$floor_can_pass)) {
  cat(
    "\n!! floor_can_pass = FALSE above: in those families NO event could pass FDR\n",
    "   via the exceedance p at this rotation count, whatever its signal. A 0-hit\n",
    "   result there is uninterpretable WITHOUT the sensitivity p below.\n"
  )
}

# (b) PRIMARY vs SENSITIVITY, side by side.
if (!"p_pooled_z" %in% names(screen_dt)) {
  cat("\nNo `p_pooled_z` column. Which of the two reasons applies:\n")
  if (!file.exists(.screen_results_file)) {
    cat(
      "  -> screen_results.csv.gz does NOT exist, so screen_dt came from the PER-EVENT\n",
      "     fallback path, which computes only a BH-proxy q. The sensitivity p needs the\n",
      "     null sidecars AND the family-stratified reference, and only 09s-aggregate.R\n",
      "     builds those. Run it once the screen completes -- nothing is stale here.\n"
    )
  } else {
    cat(
      "  -> the aggregate exists but predates the sensitivity p; re-run 09s-aggregate.R\n",
      "     (needs the screen/*_screen_null.csv.gz sidecars).\n"
    )
  }
} else if (!any(is.finite(screen_dt$p_pooled_z))) {
  cat(
    "\n`p_pooled_z` present but all NA -- the null sidecars were missing or unreadable\n",
    "when 09s-aggregate.R ran.\n"
  )
} else {
  cmp <- screen_dt[
    is.finite(p_emp),
    .(
      n_tested = .N,
      min_p_primary = signif(min(p_emp, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      min_p_pooled_z = signif(min(p_pooled_z, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      hits_primary = sum(
        is.finite(q) & q < screen_q_threshold & effect > screen_min_effect,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      hits_pooled_z = sum(
        is.finite(q_pooled_z) &
          q_pooled_z < screen_q_threshold &
          effect > screen_min_effect,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ),
    by = .by
  ]
  cat("\nHit counts and resolution, primary vs floor-free sensitivity p:\n")
  print(cmp[order(`Event Type`, feature_set)])

  # (c) EFFECT-SIZE GUARD. A large z can come from a collapsed denominator rather
  # than signal: null_R2_sd is never 0 (min ~1e-5) but can be proportionally tiny,
  # so an event with R2 = 0.005 and null sd = 3e-4 scores z = 17 on no real signal.
  # Effect size -- not null sd -- is the instrument that separates these.
  top <- screen_dt[is.finite(p_pooled_z)][order(p_pooled_z)][
    seq_len(min(15L, .N)),
    .(
      ID,
      `Event Type`,
      feature_set,
      n_samples,
      screen_R2 = signif(screen_R2, 3),
      null_R2_sd = signif(null_R2_sd, 3),
      z = round(z_screen, 1),
      effect = signif(effect, 3),
      p_pooled_z = signif(p_pooled_z, 3),
      q_pooled_z = signif(q_pooled_z, 3),
      artifact_suspect = effect < 0.01
    )
  ]
  cat(
    "\nTop events by the sensitivity p (artifact_suspect = effect < 0.01,\n",
    "i.e. z inflated by a small null sd rather than by signal):\n"
  )
  print(top)
  cat(sprintf(
    "\n%d of the top %d have effect < 0.01. screen_min_effect is currently %g;\n raise EpiATLAS_AS_SCREEN_MIN_EFFECT to exclude them from hit calls.\n",
    sum(top$artifact_suspect),
    nrow(top),
    screen_min_effect
  ))

  print(
    ggplot(
      screen_dt[is.finite(p_pooled_z) & is.finite(p_emp)],
      aes(x = p_emp, y = p_pooled_z)
    ) +
      geom_point(alpha = .2, size = .6) +
      scale_y_log10() +
      geom_hline(
        yintercept = floor_tab$bh_allows[1],
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = "firebrick"
      ) +
      facet_grid(feature_set ~ `Event Type`) +
      theme_bw() +
      labs(
        title = "Floor-free sensitivity p vs floored primary p",
        x = "Exceedance p (vertical stripe at its 1/(R+1) floor)",
        y = "Pooled-z p (log scale)",
        caption = paste(
          "The primary p piles into a vertical stripe at its floor; the sensitivity p",
          "spreads those events out. Dashed = the BH threshold the primary p could not",
          "reach. Points below it are events the floor was hiding."
        )
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "screen_floor_sensitivity.pdf"),
    width = 10,
    height = 2 + 2.2 * max(1L, uniqueN(screen_dt$feature_set)),
    limitsize = FALSE
  )
}
```

## 1.4 Per-event null distributions: the raw material behind each p-value

Everything above summarises the null by its mean and SD. This shows the null itself: for a selected
`(event, feature set)` pair, the histogram of that event's `R_used` matched-control R² values (818 for
RI, 200 for SE) with the event's own real R² drawn as a vertical line. The empirical p *is* the tail mass to the right of that line
(`p = (1 + #{null ≥ real}) / (1 + R_used)`), so the plot and the p-value are the same fact shown two ways.

*Expected for a hit:* the line sits in the far right tail, clear of the bulk.
*Expected for a fingerprint event:* the line sits inside the bulk — often at a **high absolute R²**,
which is exactly the point: the controls reach the same R².
*Deduction if a null distribution is bimodal or extremely wide:* the matched-control pool is
heterogeneous for that event (e.g. controls with very different feature availability), so its p-value is
noisier than the summary table suggests — worth checking `R_used` for that event.

A panel is an `(event, feature set)` **pair**, not an event, since the same event has a different real R²
and a different null in each space; seeing one event across its three spaces side by side is the useful
comparison. Panels are capped (all significant pairs first, then top-by-effect) and only the selected
events' sidecar files are read — the full set is tens of thousands of files.

```{r screen-null-histograms}
# Per-event null-distribution histograms: real screen_R2 (vertical line) over the
# R_used matched feature-rotation null R2 values (818 for RI, 200 for SE). These are
# the SAME quantity
# the empirical p is computed from (p = (1 + #{null >= real}) / (1 + R_used)), so
# a real line far in the right tail = small p = event-specific epigenetic signal;
# a real line buried in the bulk = fingerprint / no signal.
# Which panels to draw is decided from screen_dt ALONE, so the file selection happens
# FIRST: the full sidecar set is ~34k files / hundreds of MB at genome scale, and
# reading all of it to then plot <=24 panels dominated the render. Read only the
# events actually drawn.
#
# A facet is an (event, feature_set) PAIR, not an event — the same event has a
# different real R2 and a different null in each feature space, which is exactly the
# comparison worth seeing. Draw every significant pair, then top-by-effect, capped so
# the full-run set can't explode the grid.
max_facets <- 24L
.key <- c("ID", "feature_set")
screen_pairs <- copy(screen_dt)[, feature_set := as.character(feature_set)]
hit_pairs <- screen_pairs[sig %in% TRUE, .(ID, feature_set)]
top_pairs <- screen_pairs[is.finite(effect)][order(-effect), .(ID, feature_set)]
plot_pairs <- unique(rbindlist(list(hit_pairs, top_pairs)))
plot_pairs <- plot_pairs[seq_len(min(max_facets, nrow(plot_pairs)))]

null_files <- file.path(
  event_dir,
  "screen",
  sprintf("%d_screen_null.csv.gz", unique(plot_pairs$ID))
)
null_files <- null_files[file.exists(null_files)]

if (nrow(plot_pairs) == 0L || length(null_files) == 0L) {
  message(
    "No screen_null sidecars for the selected events — skipping per-event ",
    "null histograms. (Re-run 09s-ridge-screen.R to populate them.)"
  )
} else {
  null_long <- rbindlist(lapply(null_files, fread), fill = TRUE)
  null_long[, ID := as.integer(ID)]
  # Sidecars written before the per-feature-set screen hold the omnibus null = `long`.
  if (!"feature_set" %in% names(null_long)) {
    null_long[, feature_set := "long"]
  }
  null_long[, feature_set := as.character(feature_set)]
  null_long <- null_long[is.finite(null_R2)]

  n_omitted <- nrow(unique(screen_pairs[
    is.finite(effect),
    .(ID, feature_set)
  ])) -
    nrow(plot_pairs)
  if (n_omitted > 0L) {
    message(sprintf(
      "Null histograms: drawing %d (event × feature set) panel(s) (%d significant + top-by-effect); %d omitted.",
      nrow(plot_pairs),
      nrow(hit_pairs),
      n_omitted
    ))
  }

  nd <- null_long[plot_pairs, on = .key, nomatch = NULL]
  # Per-(event, feature_set) real value + significance + a compact facet label.
  ev_lab <- screen_pairs[
    plot_pairs,
    on = .key,
    nomatch = NULL
  ][, .(ID, feature_set, screen_R2, p_emp, q, sig)]
  ev_lab[event_dt, on = "ID", `Event Type` := `Event Type`]
  ev_lab[,
    facet := sprintf(
      "ID %d (%s) [%s]\nR2=%.3f p=%.2g q=%.2g%s",
      ID,
      `Event Type`,
      feature_set,
      screen_R2,
      p_emp,
      q,
      fifelse(sig %in% TRUE, " *", "")
    )
  ]
  nd[ev_lab, on = .key, facet := facet]
  vlines <- ev_lab[, .(ID, feature_set, facet, screen_R2, sig)]

  print(
    ggplot(nd, aes(x = null_R2)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "grey70", color = NA) +
      geom_vline(
        data = vlines,
        aes(xintercept = screen_R2, color = sig %in% TRUE),
        linewidth = 0.7
      ) +
      facet_wrap(~facet, scales = "free") +
      scale_color_manual(
        values = c(`TRUE` = "firebrick", `FALSE` = "steelblue"),
        labels = c(`TRUE` = "significant", `FALSE` = "not sig"),
        name = "real R2 (event)"
      ) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
      labs(
        title = "Tier-1: real partial-R2 vs its matched feature-rotation null (per event × feature set)",
        x = "R2 (grey = null control loci; line = this event's real R2)",
        y = "Number of null control loci",
        caption = paste(
          "One panel per (event, feature set): each grey histogram = that event's",
          "matched-control null R2 computed in THAT feature space, with the vertical",
          "line that event's own real R2 in the same space. Right-tail line = small",
          "empirical p = event-specific signal. * = FDR-significant (q < threshold",
          "FDR within tf x Event Type x feature set)."
        )
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "screen_null_histograms.pdf"),
    width = 14,
    height = 10
  )
}
```

```{r load-en-tables, eval = en_available, cache = TRUE, dependson = "load-tier1-screen"}
if (en_available) {
  # Tier-2 elastic-net per-event tables (HITS ONLY). This whole chunk is skipped
  # when en_available is FALSE (no Tier-1 hits) — see load-data — so downstream
  # EN chunks (also eval = en_available) never touch undefined/empty tables.

  # Best hyperparameters per (event, workflow)
  best_params_table <- read_event_csvs("^\\d+_best_params\\.csv\\.gz$")
  best_params_table[, ID := as.integer(ID)]
  best_params_table[,
    c("feature_set", "response") := if (.N > 0L) {
      tstrsplit(wflow_id, "_", fixed = TRUE, keep = c(1L, 2L))
    } else {
      list(character(), character()) # tstrsplit() errors on 0-row input
    }
  ]
  best_params_table[,
    response_type := fifelse(response == "PSI", "Real", "Rotated")
  ]
  best_params_table[,
    lambda_selection := factor(lambda_selection, levels = c("min", "1se"))
  ]

  # In-sample fit metrics per (event, workflow)
  fit_metrics_table <- read_event_csvs("^\\d+_fit_metrics\\.csv\\.gz$")
  fit_metrics_table[, ID := as.integer(ID)]
  fit_metrics_table[,
    c("feature_set", "response") := if (.N > 0L) {
      tstrsplit(wflow_id, "_", fixed = TRUE, keep = c(1L, 2L))
    } else {
      list(character(), character()) # tstrsplit() errors on 0-row input
    }
  ]
}
```

```{r build-cv-tables, eval = en_available, cache = TRUE, dependson = c("load-tier1-screen", "load-en-tables")}
if (en_available) {
  # cv_metrics_table: per-fold CV metrics at selected config, tagged by lambda_selection
  # cv_rsq: mean CV R² per (event, workflow) — used downstream by paired-rotation-analysis
  #         and n-robust-significance

      list(character(), character()) # tstrsplit() errors on 0-row input

  cv_metrics_table[,
    response_type := fifelse(response == "PSI", "real", "rotated")

  cv_rsq <- cv_metrics_table[
```

```{r build-summary-tables, eval = en_available, cache = TRUE, dependson = c("load-tier1-screen", "load-en-tables", "build-cv-tables")}
if (en_available) {
  # event_summary_table: one row per (event, workflow, lambda_selection).
  # Includes n_robust, expression_bias, mean CV R², rotated_hit flag.
  event_summary_table <- read_event_csvs("^\\d+_event_summary\\.csv\\.gz$")

  event_summary_table[,
```
