```{r build-summary-tables, eval = en_available, cache = TRUE, dependson = c("load-tier1-screen", "load-en-tables", "build-cv-tables")}
      tstrsplit(wflow_id, "_", fixed = TRUE, keep = c(1L, 2L))
    } else {
      list(character(), character()) # tstrsplit() errors on 0-row input
    }
  ]
  event_summary_table[,
    response_type := fifelse(response == "PSI", "real", "rotated")
  ]
  event_summary_table[
    event_dt,
    on = "ID",
    c("Event Type", "Variability", "seqnames") := .(
      `Event Type`,
      Variability,
      seqnames
    )
  ]
  event_summary_table[
    cv_rsq,
    on = .(ID, wflow_id, lambda_selection),
    mean_cv_rsq := mean_cv_rsq
  ]

  # "Rotated Hit": did this event's FEATURES get borrowed as a background control
  # for another event? (Rotation is now FEATURE-rotation — 09zz fits this event's
  # PSI against other matched events' real feature matrices — so the rotated
  # `response` token is the control event whose FEATURES were used, not whose PSI.
  # Semantics flipped from PSI-borrowing to feature-borrowing; the ID set is
  # computed the same way.)
  rotation_ids <- event_summary_table[
    response_type == "rotated",
    unique(as.integer(response))
  ]
  event_summary_table[
    response_type == "real",
    rotated_hit := fifelse(ID %in% rotation_ids, "Hit by Rotation", "Not Hit")
  ]

  # `rotation_rank` (slot index within an event's rotated models) was computed here
  # and in coef_table below. REMOVED 2026-07-30: Tier-2 fits real PSI only — the
  # rotated null moved to Tier-1 — so it was constant 0 and its only consumers
  # reduced to a plain count with an NA standard error. Nothing reads it now.

  event_summary_table[,
    feature_set := factor(feature_set, levels = c("local", "short", "long"))
  ]
  event_summary_table[,
    lambda_selection := factor(lambda_selection, levels = c("min", "1se"))
  ]
  event_summary_table[,
    Variability := factor(
      sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  ]
  event_summary_table[,
    `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)
  ]
}
```

```{r build-feature-coef-tables, eval = en_available, cache = TRUE, dependson = c("load-tier1-screen", "load-en-tables", "build-summary-tables")}
if (en_available) {
  # feature_table: features selected per CV fold per workflow.
  # coef_table: robust non-zero coefficients per workflow.
  # expression_bias is propagated from the real-PSI model for each event via the
  # ID + lambda_selection join, so rotated coef rows also carry the real model's bias label.

  feature_table <- read_event_csvs("^\\d+_fold_features\\.csv\\.gz$")
  feature_table[, ID := as.integer(ID)]
  feature_table[,
    c("feature_set", "response") := if (.N > 0L) {
      tstrsplit(wflow_id, "_", fixed = TRUE, keep = c(1L, 2L))
    } else {
      list(character(), character()) # tstrsplit() errors on 0-row input
    }
  ]
  feature_table[,
    response_type := fifelse(response == "PSI", "real", "rotated")
  ]
  feature_table[
    event_dt,
    on = "ID",
    c("Event Type", "Variability") := .(`Event Type`, Variability)
  ]
  feature_table[
    event_summary_table[
      response_type == "real",
      .(ID, lambda_selection, expression_bias)
    ],
    on = .(ID, lambda_selection),
    expression_bias := expression_bias
  ]

  coef_table <- read_event_csvs("^\\d+_nonzero_coefs\\.csv\\.gz$")
  coef_table[, ID := as.integer(ID)]
  coef_table[,
    c("feature_set", "response") := if (.N > 0L) {
      tstrsplit(wflow_id, "_", fixed = TRUE, keep = c(1L, 2L))
    } else {
      list(character(), character()) # tstrsplit() errors on 0-row input
    }
  ]
  coef_table[, response_type := fifelse(response == "PSI", "real", "rotated")]
  coef_table[
    event_dt,
    on = "ID",
    c("Event Type", "Variability") := .(`Event Type`, Variability)
  ]
  # expression_bias from real-PSI model propagated to rotated rows via ID+lambda_selection join
  coef_table[
    event_summary_table[
      response_type == "real",
      .(ID, lambda_selection, expression_bias)
    ],
    on = .(ID, lambda_selection),
    expression_bias := expression_bias
  ]
  coef_table[, let(
    c("mark", "region"),
    if (.N > 0L) {
      tstrsplit(feature, ";", fixed = TRUE)
    } else {
      list(character(), character()) # tstrsplit() errors on 0-row input
    }
  )]
  coef_table[,
    coefficient_sign := fifelse(
      coef > 0,
      "positive coefficient",
      "negative coefficient"
    )
  ]
  coef_table[,
    Response := factor(
      fifelse(response_type == "real", "Real", "Rotated"),
      levels = c("Real", "Rotated")
    )
  ]
  coef_table[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]
  for (.dt in list(feature_table, coef_table)) {
    .dt[,
      feature_set := factor(feature_set, levels = c("local", "short", "long"))
    ]
    .dt[,
      lambda_selection := factor(lambda_selection, levels = c("min", "1se"))
    ]
    .dt[,
      Variability := factor(
        sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
        levels = c("High", "Low")
      )
    ]
    .dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]
  }
}
```

```{r build-emp-p-table, eval = en_available, cache = TRUE, dependson = c("load-tier1-screen", "load-en-tables", "build-summary-tables")}
if (en_available) {
  # emp_p_dt — the bridge table between Tier 1 and Tier 2: it attaches each event's
  # SCREEN significance to each elastic-net workflow that was fit for it. Every
  # "do significant events differ in X?" analysis downstream reads this table, so it
  # is built once here rather than inside an analysis chunk.
  #
  # KEY: the join is on (ID, feature_set), NOT on ID. The screen runs in the same
  # three feature spaces the elastic-net uses, so each EN workflow gets the
  # significance of the space it was actually fit in. Joining on ID alone would both
  # triplicate every EN row (3 screen rows per event) and cross feature spaces —
  # attributing, say, a `local` screen result to a `long` model. Only
  # lambda_selection is broadcast, since the screen has no lambda analogue (it is a
  # single closed-form ridge with lambda chosen by GCV, not a regularisation path).
  #
  # `sig` = significant in THIS feature space; `sig_any` = significant in any space
  # (the Tier-2 hit definition). Use `sig` when the analysis is per-feature-set,
  # `sig_any` when it is per-event.
  fit_metrics_table[,
    response_type := fifelse(response == "PSI", "real", "rotated")
  ]
  cv_metrics_table[,
    response_type := fifelse(response == "PSI", "real", "rotated")
  ]

  fs_lambda_combos <- unique(
    best_params_table[, .(ID, feature_set, lambda_selection)]
  )
  .screen_join <- screen_dt[, .(
    ID,
    feature_set = as.character(feature_set),
    emp_p = p_emp,
    q,
    effect,
    screen_R2,
    screen_CCC,
    null_R2_mean,
    sig,
    sig_any
  )]
  emp_p_dt <- merge(
    fs_lambda_combos[, feature_set := as.character(feature_set)][],
    .screen_join,
    by = c("ID", "feature_set"),
    all.x = TRUE
  )
  emp_p_dt[event_dt, on = "ID", `Event Type` := `Event Type`]
  emp_p_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]
  # NB: EN-side ordering (local -> long, increasing window size), the reverse of
  # screen_dt's (long -> local, decreasing feature count). Downstream EN plots were
  # built against this ordering; screen plots keep theirs.
  emp_p_dt[,
    feature_set := factor(feature_set, levels = c("local", "short", "long"))
  ]
  cat(sprintf(
    "emp_p_dt: %d EN workflow rows, %d unique events, %d rows significant in their own feature space\n",
    nrow(emp_p_dt),
    uniqueN(emp_p_dt$ID),
    sum(emp_p_dt$sig %in% TRUE)
  ))
}
```

## 1.5 Detection floor: what effect size could this screen have found?

A null result is only interpretable against a stated sensitivity. Section 1.3 establishes that the
*exceedance* p is floored by the rotation count and therefore cannot reject a single event at FDR 0.1
in either event type — that is a property of the test's resolution, not of the data. This section
answers the complementary and harder question: **holding the resolution fixed, how large would a real
epigenetic effect have had to be for this screen to see it?**

**How the floor is measured.** The pipeline re-runs the *real* Tier-1 worker on a stratified sample of
real events, with the response replaced by a synthetic one built from that event's own feature matrix:

$$y_{\text{lat}} = \rho \cdot \text{(standardised linear combination of } s \text{ real feature columns)} + \sqrt{1-\rho^{2}}\cdot\varepsilon$$

Everything else — the confound set, the leave-one-ontology-supergroup-out folds, the λ rule, the matched
control rotations — is untouched, because the injected run *is* the production worker (`09s-ridge-screen.R`
under `EPIATLAS_AS_SCREEN_INJECT`), not a re-implementation. A separate implementation would drift from
`prep_event()`'s fold logic with nothing to detect it.

Three things about this design decide how the numbers below should be read:

- **ρ is a knob, not the reported quantity.** The map from ρ to achieved out-of-fold R² is strongly
  nonlinear and mode-dependent (at ρ = 1: 1.000 under a raw Gaussian response, 0.809 after a logistic
  squash, 0.518 after rank-mapping). **Always quote the achieved R², never ρ.**
- **The response is rank-mapped onto the real PSI marginal.** The injected `PSI` is the event's own
  observed PSI values re-ordered to follow $y_{\text{lat}}$, so the boundary atoms (39.3% of PSI values
  are exactly 1.0) and the bounded support are preserved exactly. This costs real recoverable signal —
  the ceiling is ≈ 0.52, not 1.0 — and that is the point: an unbounded Gaussian response would report a
  floor for a response shape PSI never has.
- **Detection is scored on `p_pooled_z`, not `p_emp`.** The exceedance p is floored, so at the sample
  size the floor sweep can afford it would measure the rotation count rather than the signal. Each
  injected event is standardised against the **real** screen's pooled-z reference — every real event's
  leave-one-out standardised null z, within its own `(Event Type × feature_set)` family — and spliced
  into that family's real p-vector to get a genuine BH rank.

**Scope.** The sweep runs on `local` only. In the `long` space the injection fails to recover a signal
that is by construction present in that space's own columns, so `long` has no measurable floor to
report — see the anchor table. That is itself a finding: the screen's power lives in the
event-overlapping features.

```{r tier1-detection-floor, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
.floor_file <- file.path(event_dir, "floor", "floor_results.csv.gz")
floor_dt <- if (file.exists(.floor_file)) fread(.floor_file) else data.table()

if (!nrow(floor_dt)) {
  cat("Detection floor not available: ", .floor_file, " is missing.\n",
    "Run `snakemake ", .floor_file, "` (the floor is in `rule all`).\n", sep = "")
} else {
  # `local` only, and this is a hard filter, not a default view: at rho = 1 the injection
  # fails to recover a signal that is by construction present in `long`'s own columns, so
  # `long` has no measurable floor to report. Pooling the spaces would average a real floor
  # against an undefined one. See the "Scope" paragraph above.
  floor_dt <- floor_dt[feature_set == "local"]
  cat(sprintf("floor sweep: %d rows, %d events, rho in {%s}\n\n",
    nrow(floor_dt), uniqueN(floor_dt$ID),
    paste(sort(unique(floor_dt$inject_rho)), collapse = ", ")))

  # ANCHORS FIRST. rho = 0 is a pure null: its detection rate must sit near the nominal
  # 10%, or the pooled-z reference is miscalibrated and nothing below it is trustworthy.
  # rho = 1 must be detected: if the strongest injectable signal is invisible, the sweep
  # is measuring a broken harness, not the screen's sensitivity.
  anch <- floor_dt[inject_rho %in% c(0, 1), .(
    n = .N,
    med_R2 = round(median(screen_R2, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    med_p_pooled_z = signif(median(p_pooled_z, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    det_rate_pct = round(100 * mean(detected, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  ), by = .(inject_rho)][order(inject_rho)]
  cat("=== anchors (rho = 0 must be near-null; rho = 1 must be detected) ===\n")
  print(anch)

  cat("\n=== detection rate vs achieved out-of-fold R2, by stratum ===\n")
  print(floor_dt[, .(
    n = .N,
    med_R2 = round(median(screen_R2, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    det_rate_pct = round(100 * mean(detected, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  ), by = .(`Event Type`, Variability, inject_rho)][order(`Event Type`, Variability, inject_rho)])

  # Power is NOT uniform across events. A blown-up statistic (|R2| > 1, 50.1% of real
  # rows) means the leave-one-group-out fit extrapolated catastrophically on at least one
  # fold; such an event cannot be rescued by a stronger signal, so pooling it with the
  # well-behaved events understates the floor for the events that actually have power.
  cat("\n=== same, stratified by blow-up |R2| > 1 (power is not uniform) ===\n")
  print(floor_dt[, .(
    n = .N,
    med_R2 = round(median(screen_R2, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    det_rate_pct = round(100 * mean(detected, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  ), by = .(`Event Type`, blowup, inject_rho)][order(`Event Type`, blowup, inject_rho)])

  cat("\n=== THE FLOOR: smallest achieved R2 detected at q_pooled_z < 0.1 ===\n")
  print(floor_dt[detected == TRUE, .(
    min_detected_R2 = round(min(screen_R2, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    med_detected_R2 = round(median(screen_R2, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    n_detected = .N
  ), by = .(`Event Type`, Variability)][order(`Event Type`, Variability)])
}
```

```{r tier1-detection-floor-curve, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.height=4.2, fig.width=8}
if (nrow(floor_dt)) {
  # Bin on the ACHIEVED R2, not on rho -- rho is the knob and the rho -> R2 map is
  # nonlinear, so a curve against rho would be a curve against an arbitrary parameter.
  .fc <- floor_dt[is.finite(screen_R2) & !is.na(detected)]
  .fc[, r2_bin := cut(screen_R2,
    breaks = c(-Inf, 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, Inf),
    labels = c("<=0", "0-0.05", "0.05-0.1", "0.1-0.2", "0.2-0.3", "0.3-0.5", ">0.5"))]
  .fcs <- .fc[, .(det = mean(detected), n = .N), by = .(`Event Type`, r2_bin)][n >= 5L]
  if (nrow(.fcs)) {
    print(
      ggplot(.fcs, aes(x = r2_bin, y = 100 * det, group = `Event Type`, colour = `Event Type`)) +
        geom_line() +
        geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
        geom_hline(yintercept = 100 * screen_q_threshold, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
        scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 4)) +
        labs(
          x = "achieved out-of-fold R² (binned)", y = "detected at q_pooled_z < 0.1 (%)",
          title = "Tier-1 detection floor (local features, rank-mapped response)",
          subtitle = sprintf("dashed line = nominal %g; bins with n < 5 dropped", screen_q_threshold)
        ) +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
    )
  } else {
    cat("too few injected rows per bin to draw the detection curve\n")
  }
}
```

**How to state this in the manuscript.** The floor is the smallest achieved out-of-fold R² that this
screen detects at FDR 0.1, per event type and variability tier, on the `local` feature space, under a
response that preserves PSI's own marginal distribution. Real events fall *below* that floor. The
correct claim is therefore: *no event's epigenetic signal exceeds the matched-locus null by more than
R² ≈ (floor), which the screen would have detected*. It is **not** *epigenetics does not influence
splicing* — a diffuse mechanism shared across loci cancels in a matched-locus null by construction
(section 1.1), and effects below the floor remain entirely possible.

# 2. Tier 2 — elastic net on the hits: which features, and how well?

Everything from here on runs **only on Tier-1 hits**, on **real PSI only** (no rotated responses), and is
gated by `en_available`. If section 1 produced no hits, the rest of this report is empty — that is the
designed behaviour, not a failure.

**What Tier 2 is and is not.** It is a *description* of the signal Tier 1 already certified: which
features, with what sign, how stably across folds. It is **not** a second significance test. Reading an
elastic-net CV R² as evidence of epigenetic control would reintroduce exactly the error Tier 1 exists to
prevent, because a good CV R² is just as achievable by fingerprint as by regulation.

**Why coefficients here need care even for genuine hits.** The features are strongly collinear
(neighbouring windows of the same mark, and all marks with cell-type identity). The elastic net will pick
one of a correlated group and zero the rest, and which one it picks can change with the fold — so
*absence* of a mark is weak evidence, and the `n_robust` / fold-consistency diagnostics in section 3 are
the guard against over-reading any single coefficient.

## 2.1 How many events have an interpretable model?

A model "exists" only if at least one feature is robustly selected in **every** CV fold
(`n_robust > 0`, i.e. `has_model == TRUE`). Events failing that are excluded from all downstream
feature-level analysis.

*Expected:* `lambda.min` (weaker regularisation) yields more selected features and therefore more events
with a model; `lambda.1se` is stricter and drops more events to `has_model == FALSE`.
*Deduction if the `min` → `1se` attrition is severe:* the selected features are only marginally
informative — they survive at the CV optimum but not once regularisation is tightened by one standard
error, so their interpretation should be treated as provisional.
*Deduction if attrition is mild:* the selected features carry enough signal to survive conservative
regularisation, which strengthens their interpretation.

Note on `rotated_hit` in these tables: it flags whether an event's **features** were borrowed as a
matched control for some other event (Tier 1's rotation is a *feature* rotation, not a PSI permutation).
It is bookkeeping about control reuse, not a result about that event.

```{r counting-events, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  event_counts <- rbindlist(
    lapply(unique(event_summary_table$lambda_selection), function(sel) {
      rbindlist(
        lapply(unique(event_summary_table$feature_set), function(fs) {
          this_summary <- event_summary_table[
            lambda_selection == sel & feature_set == fs
          ]
          modeled_ids <- this_summary[
            response_type == "real" & has_model == TRUE,
            unique(ID)
          ]
          rbindlist(
            list(
              Quantified = aggregated_dt[
                ID %in% keep_rows,
                .(N = uniqueN(ID)),
                by = `Event Type`
              ],
              Filtered = event_dt[
                ID %in% keep_rows,
                .(.N),
                by = .(`Event Type`)
              ],
              `No Model` = aggregated_dt[
                !ID %in% modeled_ids & ID %in% keep_rows,
                .(N = uniqueN(ID)),
                by = `Event Type`
              ],
              `Model` = this_summary[
                response_type == "real" & has_model == TRUE,
                .(.N),
                by = .(`Event Type`)
              ],
              `Epigenetic\nOnly Model` = this_summary[
                response_type == "real" &
                  expression_bias == "Epigenetic Only" &
                  has_model == TRUE,
                .(.N),
                by = .(`Event Type`)
              ]
            ),
            idcol = "filtering"
          )[, c("lambda_selection", "feature_set") := .(sel, fs)]
        }),
        fill = TRUE
      )
    }),
    fill = TRUE
  )

  print(event_summary_table[
    response_type == "real",
    table(expression_bias, `Event Type`, lambda_selection, feature_set)
  ])

  event_counts[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]
  event_counts[,
    feature_set := factor(feature_set, levels = c("long", "short", "local"))
  ]

  print(
    ggplot(
      event_counts,
      aes(x = N, y = reorder(filtering, N), fill = lambda_selection)
    ) +
      geom_col(position = "dodge") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        text = element_text(size = 20),
        axis.text.x = element_blank()
      ) +
      facet_grid(feature_set ~ `Event Type`, scales = "free_x") +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = N),
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
        vjust = 1.1,
        size = 4,
        angle = 90
      ) +
      labs(
        title = "Event waterfall: counts at each filtering stage",
        x = "Number of Events",
        y = NULL
      )
  )
  ggsave(file.path(plot_dir_ev, "event_counts.pdf"), width = 12, height = 5)
}
```

Events without any robust features (`has_model == FALSE`) are excluded from every downstream analysis.
Expression bias is classified on the real-PSI model and propagated to that event's other rows, so the
*Epigenetic Only* filter means the same thing everywhere it is applied.

*Deduction to draw from the proportion plots:* a large *Expression Bias* share means gene expression —
not chromatin — is carrying much of the fit for those events. Since expression tracks differentiation
state, those events cannot support a chromatin-regulation claim even if they passed Tier 1; the
*Epigenetic Only* subset is the one to interpret.

```{r generate-count-plots, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  event_summary_table[,
    Variability := factor(
      sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  ]
  event_summary_table[,
    `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)
  ]

  # Plain per-group event count. The old rotation_rank aggregation (mean/SE of the
  # per-rotation-slot counts) was removed 2026-07-30: Tier-2 fits real PSI only, so
  # every row has rotation_rank == 0, `counts` was a single value, mean() returned
  # that value unchanged and sd() returned NA — i.e. the machinery computed the plain
  # count via a detour and produced an all-NA error bar.
  event_count_dt <- event_summary_table[
    has_model == TRUE,
    .(n_events = uniqueN(ID)),
    by = .(
      `Event Type`,
      feature_set,
      response_type,
      expression_bias,
      Variability,
      lambda_selection
    )
  ]

  event_count_dt[response_type == "real", response_type := "Real"]
  event_count_dt[response_type == "rotated", response_type := "Rotated"]
  event_count_dt[,
    response_type := factor(response_type, levels = c("Real", "Rotated"))
  ]
  event_count_dt[
    expression_bias == "Expression Bias",
    expression_bias := "Expression\nBias"
  ]
  event_count_dt[
    expression_bias == "Epigenetic Only",
    expression_bias := "Epigenetic\nOnly"
  ]
  event_count_dt[
    order(Variability, decreasing = TRUE),
    cumsum_n_events := cumsum(n_events),
    by = .(
      `Event Type`,
      feature_set,
      response_type,
      expression_bias,
      lambda_selection
    )
  ]

  print(
    ggplot(
      event_count_dt,
      aes(y = n_events, x = response_type, fill = Variability)
    ) +
      geom_col() +
      ggh4x::facet_nested_wrap(
        `Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection + expression_bias
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
        legend.box = "vertical",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.title.x = element_blank()
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = variability_colors) +
      labs(
        title = "Model counts by expression bias and variability",
        y = "Number of Events"
      ) +
      NULL
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "events_rotation.png"),
    width = 16,
    height = 3,
    dpi = 600
  )
}
```
