```{r generate-proportion-plots, eval = en_available}
}
```

## 2.2 Hyperparameters actually selected

A sanity check on the tuning itself, before any coefficient is read.

*Expected:* `mixture` near 1 (lasso-like) gives sparse solutions, near 0 (ridge-like) dense ones; with
strongly collinear features the CV optimum often drifts toward the ridge end, because spreading weight
across correlated windows predicts better than committing to one.
*Deduction if `mixture` sits near 0 for most events:* the data are telling you the signal is diffuse and
not attributable to individual windows — so treat the per-feature coefficient lists in section 4 as
"which correlated group", not "which window".
*Deduction if the selected penalty is at the edge of the search grid:* the grid is truncating the
optimum and the fits are not converged in the tuning sense; widen the grid before interpreting.

The `response_type` facet is a historical artifact: Tier 2 has been real-PSI-only since the screen took
over significance, so the "rotated" panel is empty by construction.

```{r en-hyperparameters, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # How do hyperparameter choices vary across event type and feature set?
  #
  # Faceted by Event Type as well (2026-07-30): SE outnumbers RI ~18:1, so a pooled
  # panel is an SE panel and an RI-specific tuning pathology would be invisible in it.
  # The two types differ in sample size and baseline predictability, so there is no
  # reason to expect the same penalty regime. `response_type` is NOT used as a facet
  # any more — Tier-2 fits real PSI only, so it is constant and its panel was empty.
  #
  # best_params_table / fit_metrics_table come straight from 09zz's per-event CSVs and
  # carry no event metadata, so Event Type is joined on here. (`i.` cannot prefix a
  # backticked column name, hence the k_et alias.)
  .et_map <- event_dt[, .(ID = as.integer(ID), k_et = `Event Type`)]
  .bp <- copy(best_params_table)[, ID := as.integer(ID)]
  .bp[.et_map, on = "ID", `Event Type` := i.k_et]
  .bp[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]
  .fm <- copy(fit_metrics_table)[, ID := as.integer(ID)]
  .fm[.et_map, on = "ID", `Event Type` := i.k_et]
  .fm[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]

  print(
    ggplot(
      .bp[!is.na(lambda_selection)],
      aes(
        x = lambda_selection,
        y = -log10(penalty),
        color = as.factor(mixture),
        group = interaction(ID, wflow_id)
      )
    ) +
      geom_line(alpha = 0.2) +
      geom_boxplot(
        aes(group = lambda_selection),
        color = "grey30",
        fill = NA,
        outliers = FALSE
      ) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
      facet_grid(`Event Type` ~ feature_set) +
      scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "mixture") +
      labs(
        title = "Selected penalty by lambda rule, feature set, and event type",
        x = "Lambda selection rule",
        y = "-log10(penalty)"
      ) +
      theme_bw()
  )

  print(
    ggplot(
      .bp,
      aes(x = as.character(mixture), y = -log10(penalty), color = feature_set)
    ) +
      geom_boxplot(alpha = .5) +
      facet_grid(. ~ `Event Type`) +
      labs(
        title = "Penalty distribution by mixture and event type",
        x = "Mixture (0 = ridge, 1 = lasso)",
        y = "-log10(penalty)"
      ) +
      theme_bw()
  )

  # In-sample R² will be inflated by overfitting; compare to CV in paired-rotation-analysis.
  print(
    ggplot(
      .fm,
      aes(x = `Event Type`, y = .estimate, color = feature_set)
    ) +
      geom_violin(alpha = .5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
      geom_jitter(
        alpha = .2,
        position = position_jitterdodge(dodge.width = 0.8, jitter.width = 0.5),
        size = .5
      ) +
      facet_grid(.metric ~ lambda_selection, scales = "free_y") +
      labs(
        title = "In-sample fit metrics by event type (overfitting diagnostic)",
        x = "Event Type",
        y = "Fit estimate (PSI scale)"
      ) +
      main_theme(16) +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA))
  )
}
```

## 2.3 Fit quality: in-sample vs cross-validated R²

An overfitting diagnostic, not a significance test.

*Expected:* in-sample R² well above CV R², since the model was tuned on the folds it reports. The gap is
the overfitting penalty, and `lambda.1se` should show a smaller gap than `lambda.min` by construction.
*Deduction if CV R² is ≈ 0 or negative while in-sample R² is high:* the fit memorises its training folds
and transfers nothing — expected for events that only just cleared the Tier-1 threshold, and a reason not
to interpret their coefficients.
*Deduction if the gap is small and CV R² is decent:* the fit is stable across held-out ontology groups,
so its coefficients are worth interpreting.
*Deduction if `1se` does not shrink the gap:* the CV curve is flat, so the lambda choice is not doing
meaningful work and `min` vs `1se` differences elsewhere are noise.

```{r en-fit-quality, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # In-sample vs cross-validated R2 for the Tier-2 elastic-net fits — an OVERFITTING
  # diagnostic, not a significance test (significance was already settled in Tier 1).
  #
  # EXPECTATION: in-sample R2 sits well above CV R2, because the EN was tuned on the
  # same folds it reports; the gap is the overfitting penalty. Read only the CV panel
  # as a performance estimate.
  # DEDUCTION if CV R2 is near zero or negative while in-sample R2 is high: the model
  # is memorising its training folds and carries no transferable signal — expected for
  # events that only just cleared the Tier-1 threshold.
  # DEDUCTION if the gap is small AND CV R2 is decent: the fit is genuinely stable
  # across held-out ontology groups, so its coefficients are worth interpreting.
  # Note lambda.1se should show a smaller gap than lambda.min by construction (more
  # regularisation, less capacity to overfit) — if it does not, the CV curve is flat
  # and the lambda choice is not doing meaningful work.

  # Average CV folds to one value per workflow
  cv_wflow <- cv_metrics_table[
    .metric == "rsq_trad",
    .(.estimate = mean(.estimate, na.rm = TRUE)),
    by = .(ID, wflow_id, feature_set, lambda_selection, response_type)
  ]

  wflow_fit <- rbindlist(
    list(
      `In-sample` = fit_metrics_table[
        .metric == "rsq_trad",
        .(ID, wflow_id, feature_set, lambda_selection, response_type, .estimate)
      ],
      CV = cv_wflow
    ),
    idcol = "metric_type"
  )
  wflow_fit[event_dt, on = "ID", `Event Type` := `Event Type`]
  wflow_fit[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]
  wflow_fit[, metric_type := factor(metric_type, levels = c("In-sample", "CV"))]

  real_rsq_dt <- wflow_fit[
    response_type == "real",
    .(
      ID,
      `Event Type`,
      feature_set,
      lambda_selection,
      metric_type,
      real_rsq = .estimate
    )
  ]

  print(
    ggplot(
      real_rsq_dt,
      aes(x = feature_set, y = real_rsq, color = feature_set)
    ) +
      geom_violin(alpha = .5) +
      geom_jitter() +
      facet_grid(`Event Type` ~ metric_type + lambda_selection) +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
      main_theme(base_size = 16) +
      labs(
        title = "Tier-2 elastic net, real PSI: in-sample vs CV R2",
        x = NULL,
        y = "R2 (real PSI)",
        caption = paste(
          "In-sample is inflated by tuning on the same folds; only the CV panel is a",
          "performance estimate. The in-sample-minus-CV gap is the overfitting penalty."
        )
      )
  )
  ggsave(file.path(plot_dir_ev, "real_rsq.pdf"), width = 10, height = 4)
}
```

# 3. What distinguishes the significant events?

If Tier-1 significance reflects genuine event-specific regulation, it should **correlate with independent
properties** of the events — properties the screen never saw. If instead it is residual noise on top of a
fingerprint, significance should look random with respect to everything else. That is the shared logic of
this section: each analysis is a weak external validation of the hit list.

Every analysis here reads `emp_p_dt`, so `sig` is significance **in that workflow's own feature space**
(use `sig_any` for per-event statements).

**Caveat that applies throughout:** with few hits these comparisons have little power, and a null result
is then uninformative rather than evidence against H1. Read the group sizes before the p-values.

## 3.1 Do High-Variability events pass more often?

*Hypothesis:* epigenetic regulation should be most detectable where splicing actually changes across
samples, so High-Variability events should pass at a higher rate than Low-Variability ones.
*Deduction if High > Low:* consistent with regulation tracking dynamic splicing — though note it is also
consistent with a purely statistical explanation, since more PSI variance means more signal to fit.
*Deduction if the rates are equal:* significance is not tracking the dynamic range of splicing at all,
which is what one expects if it tracks cell-type identity instead.
*Caveat:* "High/Low Variability" is a between- vs within-tissue variance classification, **not** a PSI
range cutoff — both groups span the full PSI range (see section 5), so this is not a proxy for effect
size.

```{r variability-significance, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # Research question: do High-Variability events show a higher rotation-test
  # significance rate than Low-Variability events? This directly tests whether
  # epigenetic regulation is stronger for dynamically regulated splicing.

  emp_p_var_dt <- copy(emp_p_dt)
  emp_p_var_dt[
    event_dt[, .(ID, Variability)],
    on = "ID",
    Variability := Variability
  ]
  emp_p_var_dt[,
    Variability := factor(
      sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  ]
  emp_p_var_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]

  var_sig_dt <- emp_p_var_dt[
    !is.na(emp_p) & !is.na(Variability),
    .(
      n_sig = sum(sig, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_total = .N,
      pct_sig = 100 * mean(sig, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    by = .(Variability, `Event Type`, feature_set, lambda_selection)
  ]

  print(
    ggplot(var_sig_dt, aes(x = Variability, y = pct_sig, fill = feature_set)) +
      geom_col(position = "dodge") +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = sprintf("%d/%d", n_sig, n_total)),
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
        vjust = -0.3,
        size = 3
      ) +
      facet_grid(`Event Type` ~ lambda_selection) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "Tier-1 screen significance rate by splicing variability group",
        x = "Variability",
        y = "% events significant (FDR within tf x Event Type x feature set)",
        fill = "Feature set",
        caption = paste(
          "Significance is the Tier-1 ridge screen's (q < threshold), not",
          "the retired 10-rotation elastic-net p <= 1/11 test. Positive result:",
          "High-Variability bars taller than Low-Variability, consistent with epigenetic",
          "signal tracking dynamic splicing -- though more PSI variance also means more",
          "variance to fit, so this is not by itself evidence of regulation."
        )
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "variability_significance.pdf"),
    width = 8,
    height = 4
  )
}
```

## 3.2 Do significant events have more robustly selected features?

`n_robust` counts features selected in **every** CV fold, i.e. features whose usefulness survives holding
out each ontology group in turn. It is an independent stability measure: Tier 1 never saw it.

*Hypothesis:* genuine signal should be stable across held-out cell types, so significant events should
carry higher `n_robust`.
*Deduction if significant events have higher `n_robust`:* the two methods agree using different
machinery (closed-form ridge vs sparse EN across folds) — mutual corroboration, and the strongest cheap
evidence available here for H1.
*Deduction if `n_robust` is unrelated to significance:* the features driving the ridge screen are not the
ones the elastic net can pin down stably — consistent with a diffuse, collinear (fingerprint-like) signal
rather than a few specific regulatory marks.
*Deduction if significant events have systematically **lower** `n_robust`:* suspect the hits are
small-n/high-variance events where both the screen statistic and the fold-wise selection are unstable —
check against the R²-vs-n diagnostic in §1.1.

```{r n-robust-significance, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # Research question: do events with more robustly selected features (n_robust)
  # tend to pass the rotation test? n_robust counts features present in all CV
  # folds; higher n_robust = more stable, confident model.

  nrob_sig_dt <- copy(emp_p_dt)
  nrob_sig_dt[
    event_summary_table[
      response_type == "real",
      .(ID, feature_set, lambda_selection, n_robust)
    ],
    on = .(ID, feature_set, lambda_selection),
    n_robust := n_robust
  ]
  nrob_sig_dt[
    event_dt[, .(ID, Variability)],
    on = "ID",
    Variability := Variability
  ]
  nrob_sig_dt[,
    Variability := factor(
      sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  ]
  # Label reflects the Tier-1 screen's criterion (FDR within tf × Event Type ×
  # feature_set), not the retired 10-rotation elastic-net p-floor of 1/11.
  # Built once and reused by the fill scale below — a hardcoded label string there
  # silently desynchronises from this one (it did: the scale still keyed on the
  # retired "Significant (p <= 1/11)" text, so every significant violin fell through
  # to NA fill).
  .sig_lab <- sprintf("Significant (q < %g)", screen_q_threshold)
  nrob_sig_dt[
    !is.na(emp_p),
    sig_label := fifelse(sig, .sig_lab, "Not significant")
  ]
  nrob_sig_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]

  # Events with n_robust == 0 (no model) will not appear in emp_p_dt; filter is defensive
  print(
    ggplot(
      nrob_sig_dt[!is.na(n_robust) & n_robust > 0 & !is.na(sig_label)],
      aes(x = sig_label, y = n_robust, fill = sig_label)
    ) +
      geom_violin(alpha = .5, quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)) +
      geom_jitter(alpha = .15, width = 0.2, size = .5) +
      facet_grid(Variability + `Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = setNames(
          c("#D55E00", "#56B4E9"),
          c(.sig_lab, "Not significant")
        ),
        guide = "none"
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "Robust feature count by Tier-1 screen outcome",
        x = NULL,
        y = "n_robust (features selected in all CV folds)",
        caption = paste(
          "Events with n_robust = 0 (no model) excluded. Significance is the Tier-1",
          "screen's (FDR within tf x Event Type x feature_set), not the retired",
          "10-rotation elastic-net test. Positive result: significant events shifted",
          "toward higher n_robust, i.e. the two methods agree via different machinery."
        )
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "nrobust_significance.pdf"),
    width = 16,
    height = 6
  )
}
```

## 3.3 Fold-to-fold selection consistency

The same idea as `n_robust` but per *feature* rather than per event: how often is a given feature chosen
when a different ontology group is held out? Fold `0` (the full-training fit) is excluded, as it is not a
held-out fold.

*Expected under genuine locus-specific regulation:* a subset of features with high consistency — the same
marks are chosen no matter which cell types are held out.
*Expected under the fingerprint confound:* consistency spread broadly and low, because the model can
substitute any cell-type-correlated feature for any other, and which one wins depends on the fold.
*Deduction:* only high-consistency features are defensible candidates for follow-up; a feature selected
in one fold is indistinguishable from a collinear stand-in.

```{r feature-consistency, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # Research question: how consistently is each feature selected across CV folds?
  # Computed on real-PSI models only; fold "0" (full-training fit) excluded since
  # it is not a cross-validation fold.
  # High mean consistency = features robustly selected regardless of held-out tissue.

  feat_cons_dt <- feature_table[
    response_type == "real" & fold != "0",
    .(n_folds_selected = uniqueN(fold)),
    by = .(ID, wflow_id, feature_set, lambda_selection, feature, `Event Type`)
  ]
  total_folds_dt <- feature_table[
    response_type == "real" & fold != "0",
    .(total_folds = uniqueN(fold)),
    by = .(ID, wflow_id, lambda_selection)
  ]
  feat_cons_dt[
    total_folds_dt,
    on = .(ID, wflow_id, lambda_selection),
    frac_folds := n_folds_selected / total_folds
  ]

  per_event_cons_dt <- feat_cons_dt[,
    .(mean_consistency = mean(frac_folds, na.rm = TRUE)),
    by = .(ID, feature_set, lambda_selection, `Event Type`)
  ]
  per_event_cons_dt[
    event_dt[, .(ID, Variability)],
    on = "ID",
    Variability := Variability
  ]
  per_event_cons_dt[,
    Variability := factor(
      sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  ]
  per_event_cons_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]

  print(
    ggplot(
      per_event_cons_dt[!is.na(mean_consistency)],
      aes(x = mean_consistency, fill = feature_set)
    ) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 20, position = "dodge", alpha = .7) +
      facet_grid(Variability + `Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "CV fold consistency of selected features (real PSI models)",
        x = "Mean fraction of folds selecting each feature",
        y = "Number of events",
        fill = "Feature set",
        caption = "Fold 0 (full-training fit) excluded. Mean computed over all features per event. Events concentrated near 1.0 = features selected in nearly every fold (robust); near 0 = unstable, fold-sensitive selection."
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "feature_consistency.pdf"),
    width = 16,
    height = 6
  )
}
```

## 3.4 `n_robust`: real PSI vs rotated controls — **retired comparison**

**This analysis no longer has a comparison arm and is kept only for provenance.** It was written for the
old design, where each event was re-fit with the elastic net against ~10 rotated responses and
significance came from that comparison. Under the two-tier design, Tier 2 fits **real PSI only** — the
null lives entirely in Tier 1, where it is far cheaper and uses hundreds rather than ten controls — so
there are no `response_type == "rotated"` rows and the "Rotated PSI" violin is empty by construction.

The chunk therefore reports the real-PSI `n_robust` distribution only, and prints the rotated row count so
the absence is explicit rather than a silently half-drawn plot. The equivalent question — *does the real
locus beat unrelated loci?* — is answered properly in §1.2 and §1.3.

```{r n-robust-real-vs-null, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # RETIRED COMPARISON — kept for provenance, no longer has a second arm.
  # Original question: do real-PSI models robustly select more features than rotated
  # (permutation) controls? Under the two-tier design that question is answered in
  # Tier 1 (§1.2/§1.3) against HUNDREDS of matched control loci, not 10 rotated
  # responses, and Tier 2 fits real PSI ONLY — so `response_type == "rotated"` rows do
  # not exist and the "Rotated PSI" violin is empty by construction.
  # The row count is printed so the absence is explicit rather than a silently
  # half-drawn two-arm plot. Do NOT read a one-sided version of this as a result.

  nrob_comp_dt <- event_summary_table[
    !is.na(n_robust),
    .(
      ID,
      feature_set,
      lambda_selection,
      `Event Type`,
      Variability,
      response_type,
      n_robust
    )
  ]
  nrob_comp_dt[,
    Variability := factor(
      sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  ]
  nrob_comp_dt[,
    response_label := factor(
      fifelse(response_type == "real", "Real PSI", "Rotated PSI"),
      levels = c("Real PSI", "Rotated PSI")
    )
  ]
  cat(sprintf(
    "n_robust real-vs-rotated: %d real rows, %d rotated rows%s\n",
    sum(nrob_comp_dt$response_type == "real"),
    sum(nrob_comp_dt$response_type == "rotated"),
    if (sum(nrob_comp_dt$response_type == "rotated") == 0L) {
      " -- rotated arm EMPTY as expected (Tier 2 is real-PSI only); the plot below shows the real distribution only, it is NOT a comparison"
    } else {
      ""
    }
  ))
  nrob_comp_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]

  print(
    ggplot(
      nrob_comp_dt,
      aes(x = response_label, y = n_robust, fill = response_label)
    ) +
      geom_violin(alpha = .5, quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)) +
      geom_jitter(alpha = .1, width = 0.2, size = .3) +
      facet_grid(Variability + `Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c("Real PSI" = "#D55E00", "Rotated PSI" = "#56B4E9"),
        guide = "none"
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "Robust feature count: real PSI vs rotated controls",
        x = NULL,
        y = "n_robust (features selected in all CV folds)",
        caption = "Includes events with n_robust = 0 (no model built). Positive result: Real PSI distribution shifted right vs Rotated, indicating more features are robustly selected when predicting genuine splicing."
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "nrobust_real_vs_rotated.pdf"),
    width = 16,
    height = 6
  )
}
```

## 3.5 Is the result stable across the lambda rule?

A robustness check on the regularisation choice, not a biological question.

*Expected:* high concordance — events should be significant (or not) under both `min` and `1se`.
*Deduction for "min only" events:* significance depends on the weaker regularisation, so it rests on
features that do not survive a one-standard-error tightening — treat as fragile.
*Deduction for "1se only" events:* rare and slightly odd (the stricter model passing where the looser one
fails); usually a sign of an unstable CV curve for that event rather than a stronger result.
*Deduction if concordance is low overall:* the feature selection is dominated by the penalty setting
rather than by the data, and no per-event coefficient list should be reported without stating which
lambda rule produced it.

Note that Tier-1 significance itself has **no** lambda dimension (the screen's ridge λ is set by GCV, not
by a path), so any discordance here reflects the elastic-net side only.

```{r lambda-switching, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # Research question: are rotation-test results stable across lambda selection rules?
  # Concordance (both sig or both non-sig) suggests robust signal.
  # "min only" events = sensitive to regularisation; "1se only" = rare edge case.

  lambda_wide_dt <- dcast(
    emp_p_dt[!is.na(emp_p)],
    ID + feature_set + `Event Type` ~ lambda_selection,
    value.var = "sig"
  )
  setnames(lambda_wide_dt, c("min", "1se"), c("sig_min", "sig_1se"))
  lambda_wide_dt[
    event_dt[, .(ID, Variability)],
    on = "ID",
    Variability := Variability
  ]
  lambda_wide_dt[,
    Variability := factor(
      sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  ]

  lambda_wide_dt[,
    lambda_category := fcase(
      sig_min & sig_1se   , "Both significant"    ,
      sig_min & !sig_1se  , "min only"            ,
      !sig_min & sig_1se  , "1se only"            ,
      !sig_min & !sig_1se , "Neither significant"
    )
  ]
  lambda_wide_dt[,
    lambda_category := factor(
      lambda_category,
      levels = c(
        "Both significant",
        "min only",
        "1se only",
        "Neither significant"
      )
    )
  ]
  lambda_wide_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]

  lambda_summary <- lambda_wide_dt[
    !is.na(lambda_category),
    .(n = .N),
    by = .(`Event Type`, Variability, feature_set, lambda_category)
  ]
  lambda_summary[,
    pct := 100 * n / sum(n),
    by = .(`Event Type`, Variability, feature_set)
  ]

  print(
    ggplot(
      lambda_summary,
      aes(x = feature_set, y = pct, fill = lambda_category)
    ) +
      geom_col(position = "stack") +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%\n(n=%d)", pct, n)),
        position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
        size = 3
      ) +
      facet_grid(Variability ~ `Event Type`) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
          "Both significant" = "#D55E00",
          "min only" = "#E69F00",
          "1se only" = "#56B4E9",
          "Neither significant" = "#999999"
        )
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "Lambda rule concordance in Tier-1 screen significance",
        x = "Feature set",
        y = "% of events",
        fill = "Lambda significance",
        caption = paste(
          "Significance is the Tier-1 screen's. NB the screen itself has NO lambda",
          "dimension (its ridge lambda is set by GCV, not a path), so discordance here",
          "reflects the elastic-net side only. Large 'Both significant' = robust to the",
          "regularisation choice; large 'min only' = signal depends on the weaker",
          "penalty and should be treated as fragile."
        )
      )
  )
  ggsave(file.path(plot_dir_ev, "lambda_switching.pdf"), width = 8, height = 4)
}
```

# 4. Mark-level analysis: which epigenetic features get selected?

The question shifts from *which events* to *which marks*. Feature names encode both a mark and a position
(which window relative to the event), and `feature_set` distinguishes marks that overlap the event itself
(`local`) from window marks further out (`short`/`long`) — a distinction that matters for every
interpretation below, because a mark selected only in a wide window may simply be reporting a neighbouring
promoter rather than anything about the exon.

## 4.1 Which marks are selected in Epigenetic Only models?

*Hypothesis under genuine regulation:* a few marks with known splicing links should dominate —
canonically H3K36me3 (co-transcriptional, exon-biased) and DNA methylation over exon bodies.
*Hypothesis under the fingerprint confound:* selection should look like a generic "active chromatin"
mixture with no particular splicing logic, and should be broadly similar whichever events you look at.
*Deduction if selection is dominated by promoter marks (H3K4me3/H3K27ac) in wide windows only:* the models
are reading promoter/expression state, which §4.3's TSS control tests directly.
*Deduction if `local` selection is negligible while `short`/`long` selection is rich:* nothing at the exon
itself is informative, and the apparent signal comes from genomic neighbourhood — evidence against
event-level epigenetic control specifically.

```{r plot-mark-counts, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # activeChromHMM loaded per-filter in the load-session chunk above.
  # Research question: which epigenetic marks are robustly selected in Epigenetic Only models?
  # Does mark usage differ between real PSI and rotated controls?
  # Similar mark profiles for real and rotated would imply chance selection.
  activeChromHMM_dt <- data.table(
    region = activeChromHMM$name,
    chrom_state = activeChromHMM$chrom_state,
    region_width = width(activeChromHMM),
    region_ID = seq_along(activeChromHMM)
  )
  coef_table[
    activeChromHMM_dt,
    on = "region",
    c("chrom_state", "region_width", "region_ID") := .(
      chrom_state,
      region_width,
      region_ID
    )
  ]

  # Both real and rotated rows included; expression_bias was propagated from the
  # real-PSI model for each event, so the Epigenetic Only filter applies to both.
  # feature_set kept to distinguish local (event-overlapping) vs short/long window marks.
  # rotation_rank dropped 2026-07-30: Tier-2 is real-PSI only, so it was constant at 0
  # and the mean/SE across "rotation slots" reduced to the plain count with an NA SD.
  err_dt <- coef_table[
    mark != "(Intercept)" & expression_bias == "Epigenetic Only",
    .(mark = unique(mark)),
    by = .(
      ID,
      feature_set,
      response_type,
      `Event Type`,
      Variability,
      lambda_selection
    )
  ][,
    .(n_events = uniqueN(ID)),
    by = .(
      `Event Type`,
      feature_set,
      response_type,
      mark,
      Variability,
      lambda_selection
    )
  ]

  err_dt[,
    Response := factor(
      fifelse(response_type == "real", "Real", "Rotated"),
      levels = c("Real", "Rotated")
    )
  ]
  err_dt[,
    Variability := factor(
      sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  ]
  err_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = c("SE", "RI"))]
  err_dt[, mark := tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", mark))]

  hex_colors <- c(
    mark_hex_colors,
    summed_enhancer = "darkorange",
    max_promoter = "tomato"
  )
  plot_colors <- setNames(
    rep("dark grey", err_dt[, uniqueN(mark)]),
    err_dt[, unique(mark)]
  )
  names(hex_colors) <- tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", names(hex_colors)))
  for (name in names(hex_colors)) {
    inds <- startsWith(names(plot_colors), name)
    plot_colors[inds] <- hex_colors[name]
  }

  print(
    ggplot(err_dt, aes(x = Response, y = n_events, fill = mark)) +
      geom_col(position = "dodge") +
      facet_grid(
        Variability + `Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection,
        scales = "free_y"
      ) +
      labs(
        title = "Epigenetic mark usage in Epigenetic Only models",
        y = "Number of events selecting mark",
        x = NULL,
        fill = "Mark",
        caption = paste(
          "Tier-2 is real-PSI only, so there is no rotated comparison arm here; the",
          "real-vs-null question is answered in section 1. Compare local vs short/long:",
          "local marks are event-overlapping, long marks include distal elements."
        )
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      scale_fill_manual(values = plot_colors) +
      theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white")
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "mark_counts_error.pdf"),
    width = 18,
    height = 10
  )
}
```

## 4.2 Mark profiles stratified by Tier-1 significance

The sharpest version of the mark question: do events that **pass** the screen select *different* marks
from those that fail? Per mark, a Fisher's exact test compares selection frequency between the passing and
failing strata (Fisher rather than chi-squared because the passing group is small).

Three outcomes, with what each licenses:

- **POSITIVE — distinct profiles, specific marks enriched in the passing group.** Particular marks drive
  genuine epigenetic–splicing associations beyond the fingerprint, and feature interpretation is
  trustworthy for the significant subset. This is the result that would support a mechanistic claim.
- **NULL — indistinguishable profiles.** Two explanations that this comparison **cannot** separate:
  (a) all mark selection reflects cell-type identity and the passing events cleared the threshold by
  chance; or (b) genuine signal uses the *same* marks as the fingerprint, so profile comparison is blind
  to the difference. Distinguishing them needs a different design (e.g. perturbation, or matched-cell-type
  replicates), not more of this analysis.
- **CONFOUND — protocol/RNA-seq features enriched in the passing group.** Technical protocol effects, not
  epigenetics, are driving apparent signal. This is a flag to investigate, not a result.

*Power caveat, stated before the p-values:* with a small passing group, Fisher has little power, so a NULL
here is weak evidence. Check `n_group` per stratum first.

```{r mark-counts-screen-stratified, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # Research question: do events passing the rotation test select different marks
  # than failing events?
  #
  # Interpretation guide:
  #   POSITIVE — distinct profiles, mark enriched in passing group:
  #     Specific marks drive genuine epigenetic-splicing associations beyond
  #     fingerprint confound. Feature interpretation trustworthy for the
  #     significant subset.
  #
  #   NULL — similar profiles between groups:
  #     Two indistinguishable explanations at this n:
  #     (a) Fingerprint confound: all mark selection reflects cell-type identity;
  #         passing events beat the test by chance. (The old rotation-era numbers
  #         here -- min achievable p = 1/11 ≈ 9%, observed 14-15% -- no longer
  #         apply: significance is now the Tier-1 screen's FDR-controlled q.)
  #     (b) Genuine signal uses the SAME marks as the fingerprint — mark profile
  #         comparison cannot separate the two; larger n or different design needed.
  #
  #   CONFOUND signal — Protocol/RNA-seq marks enriched in passing group:
  #     Technical RNA-seq protocol effects drive apparent signal rather than
  #     epigenetic regulation. Flag for investigation.

  # Collapse Tier-1 screen significance to (ID, lambda_selection): significant if
  # ANY feature set passes (q < threshold). `sig` comes from the screen
  # via emp_p_dt, so there is no 1/11 p-floor involved any more.
  sig_collapse_dt <- emp_p_dt[,
    .(sig_any = any(sig, na.rm = TRUE)),
    by = .(ID, lambda_selection)
  ]
  sig_collapse_dt[,
    rotation_outcome := factor(
      fifelse(sig_any, "Passes Tier-1 screen", "Fails Tier-1 screen"),
      levels = c("Passes Tier-1 screen", "Fails Tier-1 screen")
    )
  ]

  coef_real_sig <- coef_table[
    response_type == "real" &
      mark != "(Intercept)" &
      expression_bias == "Epigenetic Only"
  ]
  coef_real_sig[
    sig_collapse_dt,
    on = .(ID, lambda_selection),
    rotation_outcome := rotation_outcome
  ]

  # Per event per feature_set: unique marks selected.
  # Keeping feature_set separates local (event-overlapping) from short/long window marks.
  event_mark_dt <- coef_real_sig[
    !is.na(rotation_outcome),
    .(mark = unique(mark)),
    by = .(
      ID,
      `Event Type`,
      Variability,
      feature_set,
      lambda_selection,
      rotation_outcome
    )
  ]

  # n_group: total events per stratum.
  n_group_dt <- event_mark_dt[,
    .(n_group = uniqueN(ID)),
    by = .(
      `Event Type`,
      Variability,
      feature_set,
      lambda_selection,
      rotation_outcome
    )
  ]

  err_sig_dt <- event_mark_dt[,
    .(n_events = uniqueN(ID)),
    by = .(
      `Event Type`,
      Variability,
      feature_set,
      lambda_selection,
      rotation_outcome,
      mark
    )
  ]
  err_sig_dt[
    n_group_dt,
    on = .(
      `Event Type`,
      Variability,
      feature_set,
      lambda_selection,
      rotation_outcome
    ),
    c("n_group", "pct_events") := .(n_group, 100 * n_events / n_group)
  ]

  err_sig_dt[,
    Variability := factor(
      sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  ]
  err_sig_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = c("SE", "RI"))]
  err_sig_dt[, mark := tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", mark))]

  # Fisher's exact test per mark per stratum.
  # Fisher preferred over chi-squared: passing group sizes are small.
  # Null: profiles indistinguishable → fingerprint OR same-mark genuine signal.
  # Significant enrichment in passing group: mark associated beyond fingerprint.
  fisher_dt <- err_sig_dt[,
    {
      pass_row <- .SD[rotation_outcome == "Passes Tier-1 screen"]
      fail_row <- .SD[rotation_outcome == "Fails Tier-1 screen"]
      if (nrow(pass_row) > 0L && nrow(fail_row) > 0L) {
        mat <- matrix(
          c(
            pass_row$n_events[1L],
            pass_row$n_group[1L] - pass_row$n_events[1L],
            fail_row$n_events[1L],
            fail_row$n_group[1L] - fail_row$n_events[1L]
          ),
          nrow = 2,
          dimnames = list(c("selected", "not"), c("passes", "fails"))
        )
        res <- fisher.test(mat)
        .(p_value = res$p.value, odds_ratio = unname(res$estimate))
      } else {
        .(p_value = NA_real_, odds_ratio = NA_real_)
      }
    },
    by = .(`Event Type`, Variability, feature_set, lambda_selection, mark)
  ]
  fisher_dt[, p_adj := p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")]
  fisher_dt[,
    sig_label := fcase(
      p_adj < 0.001 , "***" ,
      p_adj < 0.01  , "**"  ,
      p_adj < 0.05  , "*"   ,
      p_adj < 0.1   , "."   ,
      default = ""
    )
  ]
  print(fisher_dt[order(
    `Event Type`,
    Variability,
    feature_set,
    lambda_selection,
    p_adj
  )])

  # Annotate passing-group bars with significance label (stars above bar).
  plot_sig_dt <- err_sig_dt[rotation_outcome == "Passes Tier-1 screen"][
    fisher_dt[, .(
      `Event Type`,
      Variability,
      feature_set,
      lambda_selection,
      mark,
      sig_label
    )],
    on = .(`Event Type`, Variability, feature_set, lambda_selection, mark)
  ]

  sig_plot_colors <- setNames(
    rep("dark grey", err_sig_dt[, uniqueN(mark)]),
    err_sig_dt[, unique(mark)]
  )
  for (name in names(hex_colors)) {
    inds <- startsWith(names(sig_plot_colors), name)
    sig_plot_colors[inds] <- hex_colors[name]
  }

  print(
    ggplot(err_sig_dt, aes(x = rotation_outcome, y = pct_events, fill = mark)) +
      geom_col(position = "dodge") +
      geom_text(
        data = plot_sig_dt[sig_label != ""],
        aes(label = sig_label, y = pct_events + 3),
        position = position_dodge(0.9),
        size = 3,
        vjust = 0
      ) +
      facet_grid(
        Variability + `Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection,
        scales = "free_y"
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = sig_plot_colors) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1)
      ) +
      labs(
        title = "Mark composition by rotation test outcome (Epigenetic Only, real PSI)",
        x = NULL,
        y = "% of events in group selecting mark",
        fill = "Mark",
        caption = paste(
          "Stars above Passes bars: Fisher's exact test, BH-adjusted (. p<0.1, * p<0.05, ** p<0.01).",
          "Null (no stars, similar profiles): fingerprint confound explains selection, OR genuine",
          "signal uses same marks as fingerprint -- indistinguishable at this n.",
          "Significant enrichment in passing group: specific mark beyond fingerprint confound."
        )
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "mark_counts_rotation_stratified.pdf"),
    width = 18,
    height = 10
  )
}
```

## 4.3 TSS-proximity control for promoter-mark selection

H3K4me3 and H3K27ac are promoter marks. If events whose models select them are systematically **closer to
the TSS** than unselected events, then the selection plausibly reflects promoter chromatin leaking into the
feature window — not event-level regulation. This is a targeted confound test, not an exploratory look.

The `local` feature set is the critical comparator, and the logic is a genuine dissociation:

- **`local`, H3K4me3 selected, no TSS enrichment** → the mark genuinely overlaps the exon/intron body;
  promoter contamination is not the explanation.
- **`short`/`long`, significant TSS enrichment** → the window is capturing a nearby promoter; the mark's
  coefficient should not be read as an exon-level effect.
- **RI events near the TSS** → expected biologically (first-intron retention is common), so RI enrichment
  is not by itself evidence of contamination — interpret RI and SE separately.

The Wilcoxon test is one-tailed (`alternative = "less"`), i.e. it asks specifically whether selected events
are *closer* to the TSS, which is the direction the confound would produce.

```{r tss-proximal, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # distance_TSS: genomic distance from event to nearest TSS.
  # Event-level property — same across all samples. Take first non-NA per event.
  tss_dist_dt <- aggregated_dt[
    !is.na(distance_TSS),
    .(
      distance_TSS = distance_TSS[1L],
      abs_distance_TSS = abs(distance_TSS[1L]),
      `Event Type` = `Event Type`[1L]
    ),
    by = ID
  ]
  tss_dist_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]

  # Identify events with H3K4me3 and/or H3K27ac robustly selected.
  # Real PSI models only; all expression_bias categories (H3K4me3 may drive expression bias).
  # Stratify by feature_set and lambda_selection.
  promoter_events <- coef_table[
    response_type == "real" &
      mark %in% c("H3K4me3", "H3K27ac"),
    .(
      has_H3K4me3 = any(mark == "H3K4me3"),
      has_H3K27ac = any(mark == "H3K27ac"),
      has_either = TRUE,
      expression_bias = expression_bias[1L]
    ),
    by = .(ID, feature_set, lambda_selection)
  ]

  # Reference: all events with a fitted real-PSI model — one set per feature_set x lambda_selection.
  # Use cross-join to avoid missing events that appear in coef_table for some combos but not all.
  modeled_ids <- event_summary_table[
    response_type == "real" & has_model == TRUE,
    unique(ID)
  ]
  fs_ls_combos <- unique(promoter_events[, .(feature_set, lambda_selection)])

  combined_dt <- rbindlist(
    lapply(seq_len(nrow(fs_ls_combos)), function(i) {
      fs <- fs_ls_combos$feature_set[i]
      ls <- fs_ls_combos$lambda_selection[i]
      sel_ids <- promoter_events[
        feature_set == fs & lambda_selection == ls & has_either == TRUE,
        unique(ID)
      ]
      tss_dist_dt[
        ID %in% modeled_ids,
        .(
          ID,
          `Event Type`,
          abs_distance_TSS,
          distance_TSS,
          feature_set = fs,
          lambda_selection = ls,
          group = fifelse(
            ID %in% sel_ids,
            "H3K4me3 or H3K27ac selected",
            "Not selected"
          )
        )
      ]
    })
  )
  combined_dt[,
    group := factor(
      group,
      levels = c("H3K4me3 or H3K27ac selected", "Not selected")
    )
  ]
  combined_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]

  # --- Plot 1: Density of abs(distance_TSS), log-scale ---
  print(
    ggplot(
      combined_dt[!is.na(abs_distance_TSS)],
      aes(x = abs_distance_TSS, fill = group, color = group)
    ) +
      geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
      scale_x_log10() +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
          "H3K4me3 or H3K27ac selected" = "#D55E00",
          "Not selected" = "#56B4E9"
        ),
        name = NULL
      ) +
      scale_color_manual(
        values = c(
          "H3K4me3 or H3K27ac selected" = "#D55E00",
          "Not selected" = "#56B4E9"
        ),
        guide = "none"
      ) +
      facet_grid(`Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "TSS proximity: events with promoter marks selected vs not",
        x = "abs(distance_TSS) [bp, log10]",
        y = "Density",
        caption = paste(
          "H3K4me3 and H3K27ac are promoter-associated marks.",
          "Left shift = selected events closer to TSS than unselected.",
          "local feature set: mark overlaps exon body — strongest evidence of event-level regulation.",
          "short/long: flanking window may capture nearby promoter, not the event itself.",
          "RI events are often first-intron; TSS proximity expected and not necessarily a confound."
        )
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "tss_proximal_density.pdf"),
    width = 16,
    height = 5
  )

  # --- Plot 2: % of events within distance thresholds ---
  thresholds <- c(1000L, 2000L, 5000L, 10000L)
  thresh_dt <- rbindlist(lapply(thresholds, function(th) {
    combined_dt[
      !is.na(abs_distance_TSS),
      .(
        pct_proximal = 100 * mean(abs_distance_TSS <= th),
        n_events = .N,
        threshold_bp = th
      ),
      by = .(`Event Type`, feature_set, lambda_selection, group)
    ]
  }))
  thresh_dt[, threshold_label := paste0("<= ", threshold_bp / 1000L, " kb")]
  thresh_dt[,
    threshold_label := factor(
      threshold_label,
      levels = paste0("<= ", thresholds / 1000L, " kb")
    )
  ]

  print(
    ggplot(
      thresh_dt,
      aes(x = threshold_label, y = pct_proximal, fill = group)
    ) +
      geom_col(position = "dodge") +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%\n(n=%d)", pct_proximal, n_events)),
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
        vjust = -0.2,
        size = 2.3
      ) +
      facet_grid(`Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
          "H3K4me3 or H3K27ac selected" = "#D55E00",
          "Not selected" = "#56B4E9"
        ),
        name = NULL
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "% of events within distance threshold of TSS",
        x = "Distance threshold",
        y = "% of events"
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "tss_proximal_thresholds.pdf"),
    width = 16,
    height = 5
  )

  # --- Wilcoxon test: are selected events closer to TSS? ---
  # One-tailed: alternative = "less" tests whether selected events are *closer*.
  wilcox_dt <- combined_dt[
    !is.na(abs_distance_TSS),
    {
      sel <- .SD[group == "H3K4me3 or H3K27ac selected", abs_distance_TSS]
      nosel <- .SD[group == "Not selected", abs_distance_TSS]
      if (length(sel) >= 3L && length(nosel) >= 3L) {
        wt <- wilcox.test(sel, nosel, alternative = "less")
        .(
          p_value = wt$p.value,
          median_sel_kb = round(median(sel) / 1000, 1),
          median_ref_kb = round(median(nosel) / 1000, 1),
          n_sel = length(sel),
          n_ref = length(nosel)
        )
      } else {
        .(
          p_value = NA_real_,
          median_sel_kb = NA_real_,
          median_ref_kb = NA_real_,
          n_sel = length(sel),
          n_ref = length(nosel)
        )
      }
    },
    by = .(`Event Type`, feature_set, lambda_selection)
  ]
  wilcox_dt[, p_adj := p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")]
  wilcox_dt[,
    sig_label := fcase(
      p_adj < 0.001 , "***" ,
      p_adj < 0.01  , "**"  ,
      p_adj < 0.05  , "*"   ,
      p_adj < 0.1   , "."   ,
      default = "ns"
    )
  ]
  print(wilcox_dt[order(`Event Type`, feature_set, lambda_selection)])
}
```

# 5. PSI variability vs model quality

Does the *magnitude* of PSI change across samples predict how well an event can be modelled?

**Read the binning caveat first — and note it was previously stated wrongly.** An older comment here
claimed `aggregated_dt` is "pre-filtered to variable events, all with PSI range > 0.25". That is **false**:
there is no variance or range filter anywhere in the pipeline. The only PSI-based event filter is Wang
et al. 2024 Procedure 2 as implemented upstream in `02-3` (`psi_q95 >= 0.05 & psi_q05 <= 0.95`), which is
a **non-constitutive** test — it removes only always-excluded and always-included events, and says nothing
about how much PSI varies in between. Measured on the real `biotype_filtered` set: PSI range is ≤ 0.25 for
**33%** of events and ≤ 0.15 for 11%, and **39% of SE events have `q05 > 0.90`**, i.e. they sit hard against
the constitutive-inclusion ceiling and were retained by a margin of ≤ 0.05.

Quantile tertiles are therefore used because they are robust, **not** because the low bin is
"variable-but-less-so": the low tertile genuinely contains near-constant events, whose PSI variance is
small enough that little can be explained in principle. That matters for reading everything below —
`Variability = Low` SE events have a median range of only 0.23 — and it matters for Tier 1, where a
near-constant response is a plausible source of the wild negative group-LOO R² values seen in §1.1.

*Hypothesis (signal-strength):* larger PSI swings give more variance to explain, so high-dPSI events
should more often get a model and reach higher CV R².
*Deduction if the R²-vs-range slope is flat:* within this range, how much an event's PSI moves does not
predict how well chromatin explains it — consistent with the marks capturing static cell-type identity
rather than the intensity of dynamic regulation.
*Deduction if high-dPSI events show more Expression Bias:* gene expression co-varies with large PSI shifts
(differentiation state), so the *Epigenetic Only* label is least reliable exactly where the effect sizes are
biggest — an important caveat for any "top events" list.
*Deduction from High/Low Variability groups spanning the same PSI range:* confirms that the Variability
label captures between- vs within-tissue variance structure, **not** effect size, so §3.1 and this section
are testing different things and should not be conflated.

```{r dpsi-analysis, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # Research question: do high-dPSI events yield better models and more expression bias?
  #
  # CORRECTED 2026-07-29 — the old note here ("pre-filtered to variable splicing
  # events, all events have PSI range > 0.25") was WRONG. There is no variance/range
  # filter in the pipeline. `02-3`'s only PSI-based event filter is Wang Procedure 2,
  # `psi_q95 >= 0.05 & psi_q05 <= 0.95`, which merely drops CONSTITUTIVE events
  # (always ~0 or always ~1) and constrains variability not at all.
  # Real numbers (biotype_filtered): 33% of events have PSI range <= 0.25, 11% <= 0.15,
  # and 39% of SE events have q05 > 0.90 (retained by <= 0.05 of margin).
  # Tertile bins are used because they are robust to that skew — NOT because the low
  # bin is merely "less variable". The low bin contains genuinely near-constant events
  # with almost no variance to explain, which is a confound for any
  # "does dPSI predict model quality?" reading below.
  #
  # Interpretation guide:
  #   HIGH dPSI → more models built + higher CV R²:
  #     Signal strength drives model quality. Supports genuine epigenetic regulation.
  #
  #   NO dPSI effect on R² (flat slope in scatter):
  #     Marks capture static cell-type identity, not dynamic regulation intensity.
  #     All events are already "high change"; variation within that range is irrelevant.
  #
  #   HIGH dPSI → more expression bias:
  #     Gene expression co-varies with large PSI shifts (differentiation state), confounding
  #     epigenetic attribution. "Epigenetic Only" label may be unreliable for top-dPSI events.
  #
  #   HIGH and LOW Variability groups show similar PSI range:
  #     The "High/Low Variability" classification is NOT based on PSI range magnitude —
  #     it likely reflects relative between-tissue vs. within-tissue variation. Both groups
  #     fully overlap in absolute PSI range; the label captures a different biological axis.

  # Per-event PSI statistics.
  psi_var_dt <- aggregated_dt[
    !is.na(PSI),
    .(
      sd_psi = sd(PSI),
      range_psi = max(PSI) - min(PSI),
      n_samples = .N,
      `Event Type` = `Event Type`[1L],
      Variability = Variability[1L]
    ),
    by = ID
  ]
  psi_var_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]

  # Variability in aggregated_dt uses "High"/"Low" (not "High Variability"/"Low Variability").
  print(
    ggplot(
      psi_var_dt[!is.na(`Event Type`)],
      aes(x = Variability, y = range_psi, fill = Variability)
    ) +
      geom_violin(alpha = 0.5, quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)) +
      geom_jitter(alpha = 0.1, width = 0.2, size = 0.3) +
      facet_wrap(~`Event Type`) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c("High" = "#D55E00", "Low" = "#56B4E9"),
        guide = "none"
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "PSI range by variability group (alignment check)",
        x = NULL,
        y = "PSI range (max - min)",
        caption = paste(
          "Range = max(PSI) - min(PSI) across IHEC samples ~ max pairwise dPSI.",
          "NB: there is NO range pre-filter -- 33% of events have range <= 0.25. High/Low Variability groups overlap",
          "almost completely -- the Variability label is not based on PSI range magnitude."
        )
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "psi_range_distribution.pdf"),
    width = 6,
    height = 4
  )

  # Compute tertile bins on psi_var_dt (one row per event) BEFORE cartesian join.
  # Use -Inf/Inf as outer boundaries to avoid "breaks not unique" from probs=c(0,1) matching
  # the min/max values. Epsilon guard ensures strict monotonicity if q1==q2.
  {
    dpsi_q <- quantile(
      psi_var_dt$range_psi,
      probs = c(1 / 3, 2 / 3),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
    if (dpsi_q[[1L]] >= dpsi_q[[2L]]) {
      dpsi_q[[2L]] <- dpsi_q[[1L]] +
        .Machine$double.eps * max(1, abs(dpsi_q[[1L]])) * 1e6
    }
    psi_var_dt[,
      dpsi_bin := cut(
        range_psi,
        breaks = c(-Inf, dpsi_q[[1L]], dpsi_q[[2L]], Inf),
        labels = c(
          sprintf("Low tertile\n(<= %.2f)", dpsi_q[[1L]]),
          sprintf("Mid tertile\n(%.2f-%.2f)", dpsi_q[[1L]], dpsi_q[[2L]]),
          sprintf("High tertile\n(> %.2f)", dpsi_q[[2L]])
        ),
        include.lowest = TRUE
      )
    ]
  }

  # Join with all feature_set x lambda_selection combinations for full stratification.
  # allow.cartesian: one psi_var_dt row fans out to (n_feature_sets x n_lambda) rows.
  # dpsi_bin carried through join from psi_var_dt.
  dpsi_model_dt <- psi_var_dt[
    event_summary_table[
      response_type == "real",
      .(
        ID,
        feature_set,
        lambda_selection,
        has_model,
        expression_bias,
        n_robust,
        mean_cv_rsq
      )
    ],
    on = "ID",
    allow.cartesian = TRUE,
    nomatch = NULL
  ]
  dpsi_model_dt[,
    Variability := factor(
      sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  ]
  dpsi_model_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]

  # Model-building rate by dPSI tertile, stratified by Event Type, Variability,
  # feature_set, and lambda_selection.
  model_rate_dt <- dpsi_model_dt[
    !is.na(dpsi_bin),
    .(
      n_model = sum(has_model, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_total = .N,
      pct_model = 100 * mean(has_model, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    by = .(`Event Type`, Variability, feature_set, lambda_selection, dpsi_bin)
  ]
  print(
    ggplot(model_rate_dt, aes(x = dpsi_bin, y = pct_model, fill = dpsi_bin)) +
      geom_col() +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = sprintf("%d/%d", n_model, n_total)),
        vjust = -0.3,
        size = 2.5
      ) +
      facet_grid(Variability + `Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection) +
      scale_fill_brewer(palette = "OrRd", guide = "none") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "Model-building rate by PSI range tertile",
        x = "PSI range tertile",
        y = "% events with model (n_robust > 0)"
      )
  )
  ggsave(file.path(plot_dir_ev, "dpsi_model_rate.pdf"), width = 16, height = 8)

  # Continuous scatter: range_psi vs mean CV R² with loess trend.
  # More informative than bins given the pre-filtered range (all > 0.25).
  # Null: flat or noisy slope — PSI range within this range doesn't predict model quality.
  # Positive: upward slope — higher absolute change → better epigenetic predictability.
  print(
    ggplot(
      dpsi_model_dt[has_model == TRUE & !is.na(mean_cv_rsq)],
      aes(x = range_psi, y = mean_cv_rsq, color = Variability)
    ) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5) +
      geom_smooth(aes(group = Variability), method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
      facet_grid(`Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("High" = "#D55E00", "Low" = "#56B4E9")) +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "PSI range vs CV R2",
        x = "PSI range (max - min)",
        y = "Mean CV R2",
        caption = paste(
          "Loess trend per Variability group. Null: flat slope within the pre-filtered high-change range.",
          "No range pre-filter exists (33% of events have range <= 0.25); a flat slope means PSI range does not drive model quality."
        )
      )
  )
  ggsave(file.path(plot_dir_ev, "dpsi_cv_rsq.pdf"), width = 16, height = 5)

  # Expression bias by dPSI tertile.
  # High-dPSI events may show more expression bias if gene expression co-varies
  # with large PSI shifts (e.g., differentiation).
  bias_dt <- dpsi_model_dt[
    has_model == TRUE & !is.na(dpsi_bin) & !is.na(expression_bias),
    .(n = .N),
    by = .(
      `Event Type`,
      Variability,
      feature_set,
      lambda_selection,
      dpsi_bin,
      expression_bias
    )
  ][,
    pct := 100 * n / sum(n),
    by = .(`Event Type`, Variability, feature_set, lambda_selection, dpsi_bin)
  ]
  print(
    ggplot(bias_dt, aes(x = dpsi_bin, y = pct, fill = expression_bias)) +
      geom_col(position = "stack") +
      geom_text(
        aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%\n(n=%d)", pct, n)),
        position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
        size = 2.5
      ) +
      facet_grid(Variability + `Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
          "Epigenetic Only" = "#56B4E9",
          "Expression Bias" = "#E69F00"
        ),
        name = "Expression bias"
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "Expression bias by PSI range tertile (events with models)",
        x = "PSI range tertile",
        y = "% of events",
        caption = "Expression Bias = gene_expression feature in all CV folds."
      )
  )
  ggsave(
    file.path(plot_dir_ev, "dpsi_expression_bias.pdf"),
    width = 16,
    height = 8
  )
}
```

# 6. Inter-model feature variation: is mark selection structured, or idiosyncratic?

Final question: do event models share regulatory logic, or is each one its own story? Two views —
coefficient *signs* per mark, and mark *co-occurrence* across events.

*Hypothesis A — coherent clusters.* Groups of events share mark patterns, i.e. distinct chromatin contexts
predict splicing in distinct genomic settings (promoter-proximal vs enhancer-associated, say). Supports
genuine regulatory logic.
*Hypothesis B — no cluster structure.* Selection is idiosyncratic; no shared logic. Consistent with the
fingerprint confound, where marks enter via cell-type correlation rather than event-specific regulation.

**The co-occurrence matrix is the decisive panel, and its expected shape is the confound's fingerprint.**
If marks entered models because of local regulatory state, biologically antagonistic marks should be
*negatively* correlated — active (H3K27ac) and repressive (H3K27me3) states are largely mutually exclusive
at the same locus. An **all-positive** matrix, including for antagonistic pairs, means selection is driven
by something all marks share: cell-type identity. This mirrors the sample-axis correlation result reported
elsewhere in the project (H3K27ac vs H3K27me3 r ≈ 0.65 across samples, while the *spatial* window-axis
correlation for the same pair is negative, as biology predicts) — so the all-positive pattern here is
expected and is evidence about the confound, not a bug.

*Deduction from mixed coefficient signs for the same mark* (positive in some events, negative in others):
the mark's effect is context-dependent — e.g. H3K27ac coinciding with inclusion at one locus and exclusion
at another. Consistent sign across events would instead indicate a universal association. Mixed signs are
also, less charitably, what unstable selection among collinear features produces, so cross-check against
the fold-consistency results in §3.3 before claiming context dependence.

*Watch for r = 1.00 pairs:* these are duplicate features (identical values under two names), not two marks
that happen to agree perfectly — e.g. the `Protocol mRNA-Seq` / `Protocol total-RNA-Seq` pair.

```{r feature-heatmap, eval = en_available}
if (en_available) {
  # Research question: is mark selection structured across events, or random?
  #
  # Interpretation guide:
  #   COHERENT CLUSTERS (events group by mark pattern in heatmap):
  #     Shared epigenetic programs drive splicing prediction for groups of events.
  #     Supports genuine regulatory logic: different chromatin contexts predict
  #     splicing in different genomic contexts (e.g., promoter vs. enhancer regulated).
  #
  #   NO CLUSTER STRUCTURE (scattered heatmap):
  #     Feature selection is idiosyncratic — no shared regulatory logic across events.
  #     Consistent with fingerprint confound: marks selected via cell-type correlation,
  #     not because of event-specific epigenetic regulation.
  #
  #   ALL-POSITIVE CO-OCCURRENCE MATRIX (observed result):
  #     No negative correlations even between biologically antagonistic marks
  #     (H3K27ac active vs H3K27me3 repressive, r=0.65). This is a hallmark of
  #     fingerprint confound: all marks correlate with cell-type identity, so
  #     events where the model learns cell-type structure select ALL marks regardless
  #     of their biological antagonism. A genuine regulatory signal would show
  #     negative correlation between active and repressive marks (mutually exclusive
  #     chromatin states at the same locus).
  #     Protocol mRNA.Seq = Protocol total.RNA.Seq at r=1.00: these are duplicate
  #     features (likely same numerical values), not independent marks.
  #
  #   MIXED COEFFICIENT SIGN (same mark → + in some events, − in others):
  #     Mark effect is context-dependent. H3K27ac might activate exon inclusion in
  #     one locus and repress it in another, reflecting local regulatory architecture.
  #     Consistent sign = universal association; mixed sign = locus-specific effect.

  # All real Epigenetic Only models — stratified by Event Type, feature_set, lambda_selection.
  hm_coef_dt <- coef_table[
    response_type == "real" &
      expression_bias == "Epigenetic Only" &
      mark != "(Intercept)"
  ]
  hm_coef_dt[,
    Variability := factor(
      sub(" Variability", "", Variability, fixed = TRUE),
      levels = c("High", "Low")
    )
  ]
  hm_coef_dt[, `Event Type` := factor(`Event Type`, levels = to_analyze)]

  # --- Coefficient sign distribution -------------------------------------------
  # Stratified by Event Type (SE vs RI), feature_set (local/short/long),
  # lambda_selection (min/1se), Variability (High/Low).
  sign_dt <- hm_coef_dt[,
    .(n_pos = sum(coef > 0), n_neg = sum(coef < 0)),
    by = .(mark, `Event Type`, Variability, feature_set, lambda_selection)
  ]
  sign_dt[, `:=`(
    pct_pos = 100 * n_pos / (n_pos + n_neg),
    pct_neg = 100 * n_neg / (n_pos + n_neg)
  )]
  sign_dt[, mark := tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", mark))]
  sign_long <- melt(
    sign_dt,
    id.vars = c(
      "mark",
      "Event Type",
      "Variability",
      "feature_set",
      "lambda_selection"
    ),
    measure.vars = c("pct_pos", "pct_neg"),
    variable.name = "direction",
    value.name = "pct"
  )
  sign_long[,
    direction := fifelse(
      direction == "pct_pos",
      "Positive (+PSI)",
      "Negative (-PSI)"
    )
  ]

  print(
    ggplot(
      sign_long,
      aes(x = reorder(mark, pct), y = pct, fill = direction)
    ) +
      geom_col(position = "stack") +
      coord_flip() +
      facet_grid(Variability + `Event Type` ~ feature_set + lambda_selection) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
          "Positive (+PSI)" = "#D55E00",
          "Negative (-PSI)" = "#56B4E9"
        ),
        name = "Coefficient sign"
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA)) +
      labs(
        title = "Coefficient sign per mark (Epigenetic Only)",
        x = NULL,
        y = "% of coefficients",
        caption = paste(
          "Positive = mark associated with higher PSI (active chromatin -> exon inclusion).",
          "Negative = mark associated with lower PSI (repressive chromatin -> exon skipping).",
          "Mixed sign = context-dependent effect; consistent sign = universal association.",
          "Compare SE vs RI: RI marks may differ (intron retention context differs from exon skipping).",
          "Compare local vs long: local = event-overlapping marks; long = 500kb window (distal regulatory).",
          "High vs Low Variability: if sign profiles differ, epigenetic regulation may vary by event dynamics."
        )
      )
  )
  ggsave(file.path(plot_dir_ev, "mark_coef_sign.pdf"), width = 18, height = 10)

  # --- Mark co-occurrence correlation and sig-event heatmap --------------------
  # Loop over Event Type x feature_set x lambda_selection.
  # For each: binary presence matrix -> correlation heatmap + sig-event heatmap.
  # Expected: all-positive co-occurrence (fingerprint). Any negative correlation
  # between antagonistic marks (H3K27ac/H3K27me3) = evidence of genuine signal.

  for (et in to_analyze) {
    for (fs in c("local", "short", "long")) {
      for (ls in c("min", "1se")) {
        hm_sub <- hm_coef_dt[
          `Event Type` == et & feature_set == fs & lambda_selection == ls
        ]
        if (nrow(hm_sub) < 5L) {
          next
        }

        hm_dt_sub <- hm_sub[, .(mean_coef = mean(coef)), by = .(ID, mark)]
        all_ids_sub <- hm_dt_sub[, unique(ID)]
        all_marks_sub <- hm_dt_sub[, unique(mark)]
        pres_grid_sub <- CJ(ID = all_ids_sub, mark = all_marks_sub)
        pres_grid_sub[hm_dt_sub, on = .(ID, mark), selected := 1L]
        pres_grid_sub[is.na(selected), selected := 0L]

        pres_wide_sub <- dcast(
          pres_grid_sub,
          mark ~ ID,
          value.var = "selected",
          fill = 0L
        )
        pres_mat_sub <- as.matrix(pres_wide_sub[, -1L, with = FALSE])
        rownames(pres_mat_sub) <- pres_wide_sub$mark

        valid_marks_sub <- rownames(pres_mat_sub)[
          apply(pres_mat_sub, 1L, var) > 0
        ]
        if (length(valid_marks_sub) < 2L) {
          next
        }

        cor_mat_sub <- cor(t(pres_mat_sub[valid_marks_sub, ]))
        hc_cor_sub <- hclust(as.dist(1 - cor_mat_sub), method = "ward.D2")
        mark_ord_sub <- tools::toTitleCase(
          gsub("_", " ", rownames(cor_mat_sub)[hc_cor_sub$order])
        )
        cor_long_sub <- melt(
          data.table(mark1 = rownames(cor_mat_sub), cor_mat_sub),
          id.vars = "mark1",
          variable.name = "mark2",
          value.name = "correlation"
        )
        cor_long_sub[, `:=`(
          mark1 = factor(
            tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", mark1)),
            levels = mark_ord_sub
          ),
          mark2 = factor(
            tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", mark2)),
            levels = mark_ord_sub
          )
        )]

        p_cor_sub <- ggplot(
          cor_long_sub,
          aes(x = mark1, y = mark2, fill = correlation)
        ) +
          geom_tile(color = "white") +
          geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", correlation)), size = 2.5) +
          scale_fill_gradient2(
            low = "#56B4E9",
            mid = "white",
            high = "#D55E00",
            midpoint = 0,
            limits = c(-1, 1),
            name = "Pearson r"
          ) +
          theme_bw() +
          theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
          labs(
            title = sprintf(
              "Mark co-occurrence: %s | %s | lambda.%s (n=%d)",
              et,
              fs,
              ls,
              length(all_ids_sub)
            ),
            x = NULL,
            y = NULL,
            caption = paste(
              "All-positive = fingerprint confound signature.",
              "Negative r between active/repressive marks = genuine regulatory signal.",
              "Protocol mRNA.Seq = Protocol total.RNA.Seq (r=1.00): duplicate features."
            )
          )
        print(p_cor_sub)
        ggsave(
          file.path(
            plot_dir_ev,
            sprintf("mark_cooccurrence_%s_%s_%s.pdf", tolower(et), fs, ls)
          ),
          plot = p_cor_sub,
          width = 7,
          height = 6
        )

        # Sig-event heatmap.
        sig_ids_sub <- emp_p_dt[
          sig == TRUE & lambda_selection == ls & ID %in% all_ids_sub,
          unique(ID)
        ]
        pres_sig_sub <- pres_grid_sub[ID %in% sig_ids_sub]
        if (
          pres_sig_sub[, uniqueN(ID)] < 3L || pres_sig_sub[, uniqueN(mark)] < 3L
        ) {
          next
        }

        pres_sig_wide_sub <- dcast(
          pres_sig_sub,
          mark ~ ID,
          value.var = "selected",
          fill = 0L
        )
        pres_sig_mat_sub <- as.matrix(pres_sig_wide_sub[, -1L, with = FALSE])
        rownames(pres_sig_mat_sub) <- pres_sig_wide_sub$mark

        hc_ev_sub <- hclust(
          dist(t(pres_sig_mat_sub), method = "binary"),
          method = "ward.D2"
        )
        hc_mark_sub <- hclust(
          dist(pres_sig_mat_sub, method = "binary"),
          method = "ward.D2"
        )

        sig_long_sub <- melt(
          data.table(mark = rownames(pres_sig_mat_sub), pres_sig_mat_sub),
          id.vars = "mark",
          variable.name = "ID",
          value.name = "selected"
        )
        sig_long_sub[,
          ID := factor(
            ID,
            levels = colnames(pres_sig_mat_sub)[hc_ev_sub$order]
          )
        ]
        sig_long_sub[,
          mark := factor(
            tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", mark)),
            levels = tools::toTitleCase(
              gsub("_", " ", rownames(pres_sig_mat_sub)[hc_mark_sub$order])
            )
          )
        ]
        # Annotate Variability per event.
        sig_annot_sub <- hm_sub[
          ID %in% sig_ids_sub,
          .(ID = as.character(ID), Variability = as.character(Variability))
        ][, .SD[1L], by = ID]
        sig_long_sub[sig_annot_sub, on = "ID", Variability := Variability]

        p_hm_sub <- ggplot(
          sig_long_sub,
          aes(x = ID, y = mark, fill = factor(selected))
        ) +
          geom_tile(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
          scale_fill_manual(
            values = c("0" = "white", "1" = "#D55E00"),
            labels = c("0" = "Not selected", "1" = "Selected"),
            name = NULL
          ) +
          theme_bw() +
          theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank()) +
          labs(
            title = sprintf(
              "%d sig events: %s | %s | lambda.%s",
              pres_sig_sub[, uniqueN(ID)],
              et,
              fs,
              ls
            ),
            x = "Events (hierarchical clustering, binary distance)",
            y = NULL,
            caption = paste(
              "Coherent column blocks = shared epigenetic predictor program.",
              "Scattered = idiosyncratic selection.",
              "Clusters likely reflect cell-type fingerprint subgroups."
            )
          )
        print(p_hm_sub)
        ggsave(
          file.path(
            plot_dir_ev,
            sprintf("sig_event_mark_heatmap_%s_%s_%s.pdf", tolower(et), fs, ls)
          ),
          plot = p_hm_sub,
          width = 9,
          height = 4
        )
      }
    }
  }
}
```
